title: 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch)

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 1
summaryBullets: There was a wise man, a great artificer, and the Lord conceived love for him and received him, that he should behold the uppermost dwellings and be an eye-witness of the wise and great and inconceivable and immutable realm of God Almighty, of the very wonderful and glorious and bright and many-eyed station of the Lord's servants, and of the inaccessible throne of the Lord, and of the degrees and manifestations of the incorporeal hosts, and of the ineffable ministration of the multitude of the elements, and of the various apparition and inexpressible singing of the host of Cherubim, and of the boundless light. (1:1).
At that time, he said, when my one hundred and sixty-fifth year was completed, I begat my son Mathusal (Methuselah). (1:2).
After this too I lived two hundred years and completed of all the years of my life three hundred and sixty-five years. (1:3).
On the first day of the month I was in my house alone and was resting on my bed and slept. (1:4).
And when I was asleep, great distress came up into my heart, and I was weeping with my eyes in sleep, and I could not understand what this distress was, or what would happen to me. (1:5).

And there appeared to me two men, exceeding big, so that I never saw such on earth; their faces were shining like the sun, their eyes too (were) like a burning light, and from their lips was fire coming forth with clothing and singing of various kinds in appearance purple, their wings (were )brighter than gold, their hands whiter than snow. (1:6).
They were standing at the head of my bed and began to call me by my name. (1:7).
And I arose from my sleep and saw clearly those two men standing in front of me. (1:8).
And I saluted them and was seized with fear and the appearance of my face was changed from terror, and those men said to me: (1:9).

Have courage, Enoch, do not fear; the eternal God sent us to you, and lo! You shalt to-day ascend with us into heaven, and you shall tell your sons and all your household all that they shall do without you on earth in your house, and let no one seek you till the Lord return you to them. (1:10).

And I made haste to obey them and went out from my house, and made to the doors, as it was ordered me, and summoned my sons Mathusal (Methuselah) and Regim and Gaidad and made known to them all the marvels those (men) had told me. (1:11).
crossRefs: Genesis 5:21-24: The record of Enoch gives his years, says he walked with God after fathering Methuselah, and ends with God taking him, which is the event this book expands.
Hebrews 11:5: Enoch is listed among the faithful as the man taken so that he did not see death, and commended as having pleased God before he was taken.
Jubilees 4:17-21: The parallel account says Enoch was the first man to learn writing and wisdom, that he wrote down the signs of heaven, and that he was with the angels of God six jubilees of years.
1 Enoch 12:1-4: The other Enoch book also opens with Enoch hidden from men, his days spent with the holy ones, and the Watchers calling him the scribe of righteousness.
Daniel 10:5-12: A man appears with a face like lightning and eyes like lamps of fire, the prophet is overcome, and the first words spoken to him are Fear not.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ἑκατὸν καὶ ἑξήκοντα πέντε ἔτη (hekaton kai hexekonta pente ete)
translationNotes.note: The Hebrew text of Genesis 5:21 makes Enoch sixty-five when Methuselah was born, with three hundred years of walking with God after. The Greek Septuagint of that verse reads one hundred and sixty-five, and two hundred years after, which are the two figures this book uses. Both routes reach the same total of three hundred and sixty-five years.

The Slavonic spells Methuselah through its Greek form. Genesis 5:27 gives him nine hundred and sixty-nine years, the longest life recorded in Scripture. By the Hebrew figures in that chapter his death falls in the year the flood came.

Two sons of Enoch named only in this book. Genesis 5:22 says Enoch fathered sons and daughters besides Methuselah but names none of them. Three more brothers, Riman, Uchan and Chermion, are named later when Enoch summons his household.

The book calls Enoch's guides men, not angels, and describes them as enormous, faces shining like the sun, fire coming from their lips, wings brighter than gold and hands whiter than snow. Scripture also introduces angelic visitors as men before saying what they are, as at Genesis 18:2.

The head of the month, marked at the new moon. Numbers 10:10 sets trumpet blasts for the beginnings of the months and Numbers 28:11 sets the offering, so the date Enoch gives is a fixed marker on the calendar rather than a vague opening.

Artificer is an old English word for a skilled craftsman. Jubilees 4:17 says Enoch was the first man on earth to learn writing, knowledge and wisdom, and that he wrote down the signs of heaven; that is the kind of skill the opening line is claiming for him.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch is introduced as a wise man chosen to see the highest dwellings. He fathers Methuselah in his one hundred and sixty-fifth year, completes three hundred and sixty-five years, and two enormous shining men wake him and tell him he ascends today.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 2
summaryBullets: Listen to me, my children, I know not where I go, or what will befall me; now therefore, my children, I tell you: turn not from God before the face of the vain, who made not Heaven and earth, for these shall perish and those who worship them, and may the Lord make confident your hearts in the fear of him. And now, my children, let no one think to seek me, until the Lord return me to you. (2:1).
crossRefs: Jeremiah 10:11: The single Aramaic verse in that book says the gods who did not make the heavens and the earth will perish from the earth, which is the sentence Enoch passes to his sons.
Acts 14:15: At Lystra the crowd is told to turn from these vanities to the living God who made heaven, earth, the sea, and everything in them.
Psalm 115:4-8: The idols are silver and gold, the work of men's hands, with mouths that do not speak and eyes that do not see, and those who make them become like them.
Deuteronomy 6:13-14: A father's charge to his household in the same terms, to fear the LORD and serve him and not go after the gods of the peoples round about.
2 Kings 2:16-18: Fifty men insist on searching three days for Elijah after he is taken and find nothing, which is the search Enoch forbids in advance.

translationNotes.note: Hevel means a vapour or a breath, and Scripture uses it as a name for idols because there is nothing inside them. Jeremiah 2:5 says Israel walked after vanity and became vain, and the Greek word rendered vanities at Acts 14:15 carries the same charge.

translationNotes.term: Who made not Heaven and earth
translationNotes.original: Aramaic: אֱלָהַיָּא דִּי־שְׁמַיָּא וְאַרְקָא לָא עֲבַדוּ (elahayya di shemayya wearqa la avadu)
translationNotes.note: The test Scripture applies to any god is whether he made the world. Jeremiah 10:11 states it in Aramaic, the common speech of the Babylonian and Persian empires, and it is the only verse of that book not written in Hebrew.

A search party is the normal response when a man disappears. 2 Kings 2:16-18 records exactly that after Elijah is taken up, when fifty strong men hunt for three days and find nothing, and Enoch rules it out before he goes.

A Hebrew idiom meaning in front of or in the presence of, kept literally by the translator. It runs through the whole book, so the Lord's face, a ruler's face and an idol's face are all ways of saying in someone's presence rather than descriptions of a face.

Bayit means the house and everyone in it together: sons, wives, servants and dependants under one roof and one head. That is the group Enoch addresses, and the same sense stands behind Joshua 24:15, where a man answers for himself and his house at once.

stories.keyTakeaway: Before he goes, Enoch charges his sons not to turn from God toward the vain gods who did not make heaven and earth, warns that those gods and their worshippers will perish together, and tells his household not to search for him.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 3
summaryBullets: It came to pass, when Enoch had told his sons, that the angels took him on to their wings and bore him up on to the first heaven and placed him on the clouds. And there I looked, and again I looked higher, and saw the ether, and they placed me on the first heaven and showed me a very great Sea, greater than the earthly sea. (3:1).
crossRefs: Genesis 1:6-8: God divides the waters with a firmament and puts water above it, which is the water this chapter locates in the first heaven.
Psalm 148:4: The waters above the heavens are summoned to praise the LORD, so Scripture also speaks of water held above the sky.
Psalm 104:2-3: The LORD stretches out the heavens like a curtain, lays the beams of his chambers in the waters, and makes the clouds his chariot.
2 Corinthians 12:2: Paul writes of a man caught up as far as the third heaven, the same layered way of counting the sky that this book uses.
1 Enoch 14:8-9: The ascent in the other Enoch book also begins with clouds summoning him, lightnings speeding him, and winds lifting him upward.

translationNotes.note: One word in Hebrew and Greek covers the sky where birds fly, the space where the stars are, and the dwelling of God. This book sorts them into ten layers and climbs from the bottom, so heaven here means the lowest of them and not the throne room.
Aither is the bright upper air, which Greek writers kept distinct from aer, the thicker air near the ground. The translator kept the Greek word. It names a clear high region, not empty space.

The water above the firmament. Genesis 1:7 divides the waters under the firmament from the waters above it, and Genesis 7:11 says the windows of heaven were opened when the flood came, so the upper water is treated as real and held back.

Scripture gives wings to the cherubim and the seraphim but never describes ordinary angels carrying a man aloft on them. That detail belongs to this book. Exodus 19:4 uses wings differently, of God bearing Israel out of Egypt on eagles' wings.

The cloud is where God shows himself in the wilderness, leading the camp at Exodus 13:21 and filling the tabernacle at Exodus 40:34. Setting Enoch on the clouds puts him at the edge of that territory before the climb begins.

stories.keyTakeaway: The angels carry Enoch on their wings to the first heaven and set him on the clouds, where he looks up through the ether and is shown a sea greater than any sea on earth.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 4
summaryBullets: They brought before my face the elders and rulers of the stellar orders, and showed me two hundred angels, who rule the stars and (their) services to the heavens, and fly with their wings and come round all those who sail. (4:1).
crossRefs: Job 38:31-33: God asks whether a man can bind the Pleiades, guide Arcturus, or knows the ordinances of heaven, which is the government this chapter hands to angels.
Isaiah 40:26: The LORD brings out the host of the stars by number, calls them all by name, and not one of them is missing.
Psalm 147:4: He tells the number of the stars and gives every one of them a name.
Deuteronomy 4:19: Israel is warned not to look up at the sun, moon and stars and be drawn away to worship them, since they were given to all the nations under heaven.
1 Enoch 82:9-13: The other Enoch book names leaders set over the divisions of the year and the stations of the stars, the same kind of office described here.

translationNotes.note: The word names an office, not an age. Elders were the senior men who sat at the town gate and settled cases, so calling these beings elders means rank and authority over the star orders. Revelation 4:4 seats twenty-four elders round the throne with the same sense.

Scripture puts the ordering of the lights in God's own hand, at Genesis 1:16 and Isaiah 40:26, and names no angelic rulers over them. The two hundred angels who rule the stars are supplied by this book.

Shipping in the Mediterranean largely stopped for the winter, and Acts 27:9 marks the point in the year when sailing turned dangerous. Crews steered by sun and stars, which is why Acts 27:20 counts it a catastrophe that neither appeared for many days.

Scripture uses stars both for the lights themselves and for living beings, as at Job 38:7 where the morning stars sing together and the sons of God shout. This chapter holds both senses at once by putting angels in charge of the lights.

Avodah means work and worship in the same breath, and it is the word for the priests' duty at the tabernacle. Applied to the stars it makes their courses a form of service, which is how Psalm 19:1-2 has the sky telling God's glory day and night without speech.

stories.keyTakeaway: In the first heaven Enoch is shown the elders and rulers of the star orders, two hundred angels who govern the stars and their service, and who fly round over everyone at sea.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 5
summaryBullets: And here I looked down and saw the treasure-houses of the snow, and the angels who keep their terrible store-houses, and the clouds from where they come out and into which they go. (5:1).
crossRefs: Job 38:22-23: God asks whether a man has entered the treasures of the snow and the hail, which are held in reserve against the day of battle and war.
Psalm 135:7: He raises vapours from the ends of the earth, makes lightnings for the rain, and brings the wind out of his treasuries.
Job 37:6: God says to the snow, Be thou on the earth, and to the rain likewise, so the weather is issued as a direct order.
Psalm 147:16-17: He gives snow like wool, scatters the hoar frost like ashes, and casts out his ice like morsels.

1 Enoch 60:11-21: The other Enoch book lists spirits set over the thunder, the lightning, the hail, the hoar frost, the mist, the dew and the rain, the same arrangement of stored weather with keepers.

translationNotes.note: An otsar is a strongroom, the place a palace or temple kept grain, oil, silver and weapons under lock and a keeper. Job 38:22 uses that word of snow and hail, so the picture is a guarded warehouse rather than a figure of speech about weather.

Snow is rare in the lowlands of Israel and ordinary on the heights, and Mount Hermon carries it above nine thousand feet for much of the year. 2 Samuel 23:20 records Benaiah killing a lion in a pit on a snowy day as a feat worth writing down.

Each store in this book has a keeper who opens and shuts it. Scripture puts snow, hail and storm wind directly under God's word, as at Job 37:6 and Psalm 148:8, and names no keepers. The keepers come from this book.

translationNotes.term: The clouds from where they come out
translationNotes.note: Clouds were watched coming off the sea and understood as the visible carrier of stored water. 1 Kings 18:44 has Elijah's servant report a cloud the size of a man's hand rising out of the sea, and that was enough to know the rain had started.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch looks down from the first heaven and sees the storehouses where snow is kept, the angels who guard them, and the clouds the snow comes out of and returns into.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 6
summaryBullets: They showed me the treasure-house of the dew, like oil of the olive, and the appearance of its form, as of all the flowers of the earth; further many angels guarding the treasure-houses of these (things), and how they are made to shut and open. (6:1).
crossRefs: Genesis 27:28: Isaac's blessing asks God to give of the dew of heaven and the fatness of the earth, so dew is something granted rather than assumed.
Deuteronomy 33:28: The blessing on Israel pictures a land of corn and wine where the heavens drop down dew.
Judges 6:36-40: Gideon lays a fleece on the threshing floor twice, wet with dew on dry ground and then dry on wet ground, so dew is shown under direct control.
Exodus 16:13-14: The manna is found with the morning dew, a small round thing lying on the wilderness once the dew had gone up.
Hosea 14:5: God says he will be as the dew to Israel, so that he shall grow as the lily and strike his roots like Lebanon.

translationNotes.note: Rain in Israel stops from about mid-May to mid-October, and heavy night dew off the sea is a genuine water source through those dry months. Losing it is a curse, which is why Elijah's word at 1 Kings 17:1 withholds dew before it withholds rain.

Olive oil was food, lamp fuel, medicine and anointing all at once. Exodus 27:20 requires pure beaten oil for the lamp, meaning the first pressing taken by crushing the fruit without heat, and that is the grade of oil the dew is being compared to.

The store does not run itself; this book gives angels the key, as it did for the snow one chapter earlier. Deuteronomy 28:12 speaks of the LORD opening his good treasure the heaven to give rain in its season, with no keeper named.

translationNotes.term: All the flowers of the earth
translationNotes.note: Wild flowers cover the hills of Israel for a few weeks after the winter rains and then burn off. Isaiah 40:6-8 and Matthew 6:28-30 both build on that short season, so comparing the dew store to every flower at once packs a whole spring into one image.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch is shown the storehouse of the dew, which looks like olive oil and carries the appearance of every flower on earth, with many angels who guard it and control when it opens and shuts.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 7
summaryBullets: And those men took me and led me up on to the second heaven, and showed me darkness, greater than earthly darkness, and there I saw prisoners hanging, watched, awaiting the great and boundless judgment, and these angels (spirits) were dark-looking, more than earthly darkness, and incessantly making weeping through all hours. (7:1).

And I said to the men who were with me: Wherefore are these incessantly tortured? They answered me: These are God's apostates, who obeyed not God's commands, but took counsel with their own will, and turned away with their prince, who also (is) fastened on the fifth heaven. (7:2).

And I felt great pity for them, and they saluted me, and said to me: Man of God, pray for us to the Lord; and I answered to them: Who am I, a mortal man, that I should pray for angels (spirits)? Who knows where I go, or what will befall me? Or who will pray for me? (7:3).
crossRefs: 2 Peter 2:4: God did not spare the angels that sinned but cast them down and delivered them into chains of darkness, reserved for judgment.
Jude 1:6: The angels who did not keep their first estate are held in everlasting chains under darkness until the judgment of the great day.
1 Enoch 21:7-10: Enoch is shown a place of fire beyond measure and told it is the prison of the angels, where they are held for ever.
1 Enoch 13:4-7: The Watchers beg Enoch to draw up a petition for them and read it before the Lord, because they can no longer lift their own eyes to heaven.
Isaiah 24:21-22: The host of the high ones is gathered as prisoners are gathered in a pit, shut up in prison, and after many days visited.

translationNotes.note: The Greek noun means a standing away, and it was the ordinary word for political revolt as much as for abandoning a faith. The text defines the crime in its next clause: they took counsel with their own will instead of obeying God's commands.

He is not named in this chapter, and all the text says is that he is fastened on the fifth heaven, three levels above these prisoners. Enoch reaches the fifth heaven later in the ascent, and the book names him there.

They are described as hung under guard rather than shut in a pit. 1 Enoch 18:12-16 gives a similar scene, seven stars bound together like great mountains and burning, held in a prison for not coming out at their appointed times.

translationNotes.term: Who am I, a mortal man
translationNotes.note: Enoch refuses to intercede. In 1 Enoch 13:4-7 he accepts the same request and writes the petition, and the answer returned in 1 Enoch 14:4-7 is that they will have no peace and no forgiveness. This book has him decline before he starts.

The day is being divided into hours, twelve of them between sunrise and sunset, so the hours are longer in summer than in winter. John 11:9 uses that same twelve-hour day, and Mark 13:35 names the four watches that split the night.

stories.keyTakeaway: The second heaven holds darkness and hanging prisoners who weep without pause. Enoch is told they are apostate angels who followed their prince, and when they beg him to pray for them he answers that he is a mortal man who does not know his own end.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 8
summaryBullets: And those men took me from there, and led me up on to the third heaven, and placed me there; and I looked downwards, and saw the produce of these places, such as has never been known for goodness. (8:1).
And I saw all the sweet-flowering trees and beheld their fruits, which were sweet-smelling, and all the foods borne (by them) bubbling with fragrant exhalation. (8:2).

And in the midst of the trees that of life, in that place whereon the Lord rests, when he goes up into paradise; and this tree is of ineffable goodness and fragrance, and adorned more than every existing thing; and on all sides (it is) in form gold-looking and vermilion and fire-like and covers all, and it has produce from all fruits. (8:3).
Its root is in the garden at the earth's end. (8:4).
And paradise is between corruptibility and incorruptibility. (8:5).

And two springs come out which send forth honey and milk, and their springs send forth oil and wine, and they separate into four parts, and go round with quiet course, and go down into the PARADISE OF EDEN, between corruptibility and incorruptibility. (8:6).
And from there they go forth along the earth, and have a revolution to their circle even as other elements. (8:7).
And here there is no unfruitful tree, and every place is blessed. (8:8).
And (there are) three hundred angels very bright, who keep the garden, and with incessant sweet singing and never-silent voices serve the Lord throughout all days and hours. (8:9).
And I said: How very sweet is this place, and those men said to me: (8:10).
crossRefs: Genesis 2:8-10: God plants a garden eastward in Eden with the tree of life in the middle, and a river goes out of Eden and parts into four heads.
2 Corinthians 12:2-4: Paul writes of a man caught up to the third heaven and into paradise, where he heard words a man is not permitted to repeat.
Revelation 22:1-2: A river of water of life comes from the throne, and the tree of life stands on both sides of it bearing twelve kinds of fruit.
Ezekiel 47:12: Trees grow on both banks of the river from the sanctuary, their fruit never fails, they bear every month, and their leaves are for medicine.
1 Enoch 32:3-6: Enoch is brought to the garden of righteousness and shown the tree of wisdom whose fruit Adam and Eve ate before they were driven out.

translationNotes.note: The Greek word is borrowed from Old Persian and means a walled park or hunting preserve belonging to a king. The Septuagint uses it for the garden of Genesis 2:8, and the Hebrew form stands at Nehemiah 2:8 for the king's forest and at Ecclesiastes 2:5 for orchards a man plants.

The pair means perishable and imperishable. Paul sets the same two words against each other at 1 Corinthians 15:53, where the corruptible must put on incorruption. This book locates paradise on the border between the two conditions rather than in either one.

translationNotes.term: Its root is in the garden at the earth's end
translationNotes.note: The book puts the tree of life in the third heaven while its root stays in the earthly garden, joining the two places by one tree. Genesis 2:9 sets the tree in the garden on earth and Revelation 22:2 sets it beside the throne; the joining root is supplied here.

translationNotes.term: Honey and milk, oil and wine
translationNotes.note: These four are the staples of the land rather than luxuries. Milk and honey name the promised land at Exodus 3:8, and corn, new wine and oil are the standard harvest triple at Deuteronomy 11:14. Springs running with them is a picture of harvest without labour.

The book counts the garden's keepers. Genesis 3:24 stations cherubim and a flaming sword turning every way at the east of the garden to guard the way to the tree of life, and gives no number for them.

stories.keyTakeaway: The third heaven is paradise, full of sweet-smelling trees with the tree of life at its centre, fed by springs that run with honey, milk, oil and wine and divide into four, and kept by three hundred singing angels.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 9
summaryBullets: This place, O Enoch, is prepared for the righteous, who endure all manner of offence from those that exasperate their souls, who avert their eyes from iniquity, and make righteous judgment, and give bread to the hungering, and cover the naked with clothing, and raise up the fallen, and help injured orphans, and who walk without fault before the face of the Lord, and serve him alone, and for them is prepared this place for eternal inheritance. (9:1).
crossRefs: Isaiah 58:6-7: The fast God chooses is to loose the bands of wickedness, deal bread to the hungry, bring the poor into the house, and cover the naked.
Ezekiel 18:5-9: The righteous man is defined entirely by conduct, giving bread to the hungry, covering the naked, taking no interest and executing true judgment.
Job 31:16-22: Job swears he never withheld from the poor, never ate his morsel alone, and never lifted his hand against the fatherless.
Matthew 25:35-40: The verdict turns on feeding, giving drink, taking in the stranger, clothing the naked, and visiting the sick and the imprisoned.
Tobit 4:16-17: A father tells his son to give his bread to the hungry and his garments to the naked, and to pour out his bread on the burial of the just.

translationNotes.note: Both words come out of the courtroom and mean the party a judge finds for, the one in the right. The list in this verse is a description of conduct that a court could check, not a description of how a man feels.

Cases were heard by elders sitting in the open gateway of the town, so judging honestly was a duty of ordinary men and not of officials only. Deuteronomy 16:18-20 orders judges in every gate and bans bribes, and Ruth 4:1-2 shows the procedure with ten elders called to the gate.

An orphan here is a child with no father, and so with nobody to press his claim in court or hold his land for him. Exodus 22:22-24 threatens direct judgment on anyone who afflicts the fatherless or the widow, and Deuteronomy 24:17 forbids taking a widow's garment in pledge.

Cloth was expensive and a cloak was often a poor man's largest possession and his blanket. Exodus 22:26-27 requires a cloak taken as security for a loan to be handed back before sunset, because the man has nothing else to sleep in.

A nachalah is the family land holding that could not be sold away for good and returned to the family at the jubilee under Leviticus 25:23-28. Calling paradise an inheritance borrows the language of land tenure: a portion held by right and handed down.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch is told that this place is prepared for the righteous, and the list defining them is practical: they endure insult, turn their eyes from wrong, judge honestly, feed the hungry, clothe the naked, lift the fallen and defend orphans.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 10
summaryBullets: And those two men led me up on to the Northern side, and showed me there a very terrible place, and (there were) all manner of tortures in that place: cruel darkness and unillumined gloom, and there is no light there, but murky fire constantly flaming aloft, and (there is) a fiery river coming forth, and that whole place is everywhere fire, and everywhere (there is) frost and ice, thirst and shivering, while the bonds are very cruel, and the angels (spirits) fearful and merciless, bearing angry weapons, merciless torture, and I said: (10:1).
Woe, woe, how very terrible is this place. (10:2).

And those men said to me: This place, O Enoch, is prepared for those who dishonour God, who on earth practice sin against nature, which is child-corruption after the sodomitic fashion, magic-making, enchantments and devilish witchcrafts, and who boast of their wicked deeds, stealing, lies, calumnies, envy, rancour, fornication, murder, and who, accursed, steal the souls of men, who, seeing the poor take away their goods and themselves wax rich, injuring them for other men's goods; who being able to satisfy the empty, made the hungering to die; being able to clothe, stripped the naked; and who knew not their creator, and bowed to the soulless (and lifeless) gods, who cannot see nor hear, vain gods, (who also) built hewn images and bow down to unclean handiwork, for all these is prepared this place among these, for eternal inheritance. (10:3).
crossRefs: Isaiah 66:24: The book closes on the carcases of the men who transgressed, where their worm does not die and their fire is not quenched.
Matthew 25:41: The sentence in the parable sends the condemned away into everlasting fire prepared for the devil and his angels.

Deuteronomy 18:9-12: The practices of the nations are listed one by one, passing a child through the fire, divination, enchantment, witchcraft and consulting the dead, and every one is called an abomination.
Revelation 21:8: The excluded are named as the fearful, unbelieving, abominable, murderers, whoremongers, sorcerers, idolaters and liars.
Ezekiel 22:6-12: The charge sheet against Jerusalem runs the same way, from oppressing the stranger and the fatherless to taking interest and shedding blood for gain.

translationNotes.note: This is the wording of the English translation W. R. Morfill made in 1896. The Greek term behind the idea means the corruption of boys, that is the sexual use of children by men, and it stands as its own item in early vice lists; the Didache, at chapter two, forbids it in a single command set beside adultery and murder.

Against nature is the phrase Paul uses at Romans 1:26, where women and men are described exchanging natural use for what is against nature. This book uses it as the heading over the sexual crimes it then names.

Kashaph is the verb behind sorcerer and witch in the Old Testament. The Greek pharmakeia covers drugs, potions and spells together, and it is the word rendered witchcraft at Galatians 5:20. Exodus 22:18 makes the practice a capital crime in Israel.

translationNotes.term: Who steal the souls of men
translationNotes.note: The phrase stands between murder and robbing the poor. Scripture treats stealing a man and selling him as a capital crime at Exodus 21:16 and Deuteronomy 24:7, which outlaws the slave trade at its source, and 1 Timothy 1:10 lists menstealers alongside murderers and perjurers.

North is the direction the threat comes from in Scripture, because the invasion road ran down that way. Jeremiah 1:14 says out of the north an evil shall break forth on all the inhabitants of the land, and Isaiah 14:13 puts the boast about a throne in the sides of the north.

This place holds murky flame, a fiery river, frost, ice and shivering at once. Scripture describes the punishment as unquenchable fire at Isaiah 66:24 and as outer darkness with weeping at Matthew 8:12. Fire combined with cold is this book's own picture.

stories.keyTakeaway: On the northern side Enoch is shown a place of torment holding fire, frost and merciless guards, and he is given the list of what puts a person there, running from sexual crime and sorcery through theft and murder to robbing the poor and idol worship.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 11
summaryBullets: Those men took me, and led me up on to the fourth heaven, and showed me all the successive goings, and all the rays of the light of sun and moon. (11:1).
And I measure their goings, and compared their light, and saw that the sun's light is greater than the moon's. (11:2).
Its circle and the wheels on which it goes always, like the wind going past with very marvellous speed, and day and night it has no rest. (11:3).

Its passage and return (are accompanied by) four great stars, (and) each star has under it a thousand stars, to the right of the sun's wheel, (and by) four to the left, each having under it a thousand stars, altogether eight thousand, issuing with the sun continually. (11:4).
And by day fifteen myriads of angels attend it, and by night A thousand. (11:5).
And six-winged ones issue with the angels before the sun's wheel into the fiery flames, and a hundred angels kindle the sun and set it alight. (11:6).
crossRefs: Genesis 1:14-18: The lights are set in the firmament to divide day from night and to mark signs, seasons, days and years, with the greater light given rule over the day.
Psalm 19:4-6: The sun has a tabernacle set for it, comes out like a bridegroom, and runs his circuit from one end of heaven to the other.
Ecclesiastes 1:5: The sun rises, goes down, and hurries back to the place where it rose, a circuit with no rest in it.
Daniel 7:10: A thousand thousands minister before the throne and ten thousand times ten thousand stand there, the scale on which these attendants are counted.
1 Enoch 72:2-6: The other Enoch book also opens the sun's account with its chariot, the wind that drives it, and the portals it rises through.

translationNotes.note: A myriad is ten thousand, the largest number Greek had a single word for. Fifteen myriads is one hundred and fifty thousand angels attending the sun by day against a thousand by night. Revelation 5:11 uses the same unit doubled, ten thousand times ten thousand.

The count comes from four great stars on each side of the sun's wheel with a thousand under each. For comparison, about six thousand stars in the whole sky are bright enough to see without a telescope, and only half of those stand above the horizon at any moment.

The sun is pictured riding a wheeled vehicle, the ordinary ancient image for its daily track. That was not only a picture: 2 Kings 23:11 records horses and chariots dedicated to the sun standing at the entrance of the temple in Jerusalem, and Josiah burned the chariots.

The six-winged ones are the seraphim, named for the wings Isaiah 6:2 counts, two covering the face, two the feet and two for flying. The Slavonic keeps the description rather than the title, so the same beings appear under two names in this book.

translationNotes.term: A hundred angels kindle the sun
translationNotes.note: The book has the sun lit each morning by a working party rather than burning of itself. Genesis 1:16 has God make the two great lights and gives them no attendants. The kindling crew, like the counts of angels through these chapters, is supplied here.

stories.keyTakeaway: In the fourth heaven Enoch is shown the courses of the sun and moon and measures them himself, finding the sun the brighter. Eight thousand stars ride with the sun's wheel, angels attend it in their thousands, and a hundred angels set it alight.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 12
summaryBullets: And I looked and saw other flying elements of the sun, whose names (are) Phoenixes and Chalkydri, marvellous and wonderful, with feet and tails in the form of a lion, and a crocodile's head, their appearance (is) empurpled, like the rainbow; their size (is) nine hundred measures, their wings (are like) those of angels, each (has) twelve, and they attend and accompany the sun, bearing heat and dew, as it is ordered them from God. (12:1).
Thus (the sun) revolves and goes, and rises under the heaven, and its course goes under the earth with the light of its rays incessantly. (12:2).
crossRefs: Isaiah 6:2: The seraphim above the throne each have six wings, which is the wing count Scripture gives the creatures nearest God.
Revelation 4:6-8: The four living creatures round the throne are covered with eyes and have six wings each, and they rest neither day nor night.
Psalm 104:19-23: The sun knows his going down, God makes darkness and it is night, and at sunrise men go out to their work until the evening.
Job 26:7-10: God stretches out the north over empty space, hangs the earth upon nothing, and has drawn a boundary on the waters until day and night come to an end.
1 Enoch 72:5: In the other Enoch book the sun's chariot is driven by the wind and returns through the north to reach the east, not under the earth.

translationNotes.note: One Greek word covers the crimson dye, the date palm and a bird. Herodotus, in the second book of his Histories, reports what the Egyptians at Heliopolis told him about a bird that came once in five hundred years carrying its dead parent packed in myrrh, and adds that he had only seen it in a painting.

The name is a Greek compound of chalkos, bronze, and hydra, a water-snake, so it means bronze serpents. The description then mixes a lion's feet and tail with a crocodile's head and twelve wings. No such creature appears in Scripture.

The text gives a number and no unit, and the translation says measures because the Slavonic does not identify what is being counted. The figure cannot be converted into modern lengths. What it conveys is size, not a dimension a reader can check.

translationNotes.term: Its course goes under the earth
translationNotes.note: The book has the sun travel beneath the earth through the night and rise again in the east, which is the older Egyptian and Mesopotamian picture. Scripture reports sunrise and sunset without describing the route between them.

These are the two things the sun governs in a farming year. Heat ripens the grain and can burn a crop off if it comes early, and the night dew that keeps plants alive through the rainless summer forms only after the ground cools. Genesis 8:22 fixes heat and cold, summer and winter as a standing order.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch sees the flying creatures that travel with the sun, the Phoenixes and Chalkydri, with lion feet and tails, crocodile heads, rainbow colouring and twelve wings each, and he watches the sun pass beneath the earth at night.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 13
summaryBullets: Those men bore me away to the east, and placed me at the sun's gates, where the sun goes forth according to the regulation of the seasons and the circuit of the months of the whole year, and the number of the hours day and night. (13:1).

And I saw six gates open, each gate having sixty-one stadia and A quarter of one stadium, and I measured (them) truly, and understood their size (to be) so much, through which the sun goes forth, and goes to the west, and is made even, and rises throughout all the months, and turns back again from the six gates according to the succession of the seasons; thus (the period) of the whole year is finished after the returns of the four seasons. (13:2).
crossRefs: Psalm 19:4-6: A tabernacle is set for the sun in the heavens, and it goes out from one end of heaven with its circuit to the other end.
Job 38:12-13: God asks whether Job has ever commanded the morning and made the dayspring know its place, so the point of sunrise is treated as assigned rather than accidental.
Genesis 1:14: The lights in the firmament are set to divide day from night and to serve as signs for seasons, days and years.
Ecclesiastes 1:5: The sun rises and goes down and hastens back to the place where it arose, the circuit these gates are said to govern.
1 Enoch 72:2-7: The other Enoch book counts six portals in the east through which the sun rises and six in the west where it sets, the same arrangement measured here.

translationNotes.note: A stadion is about six hundred Greek feet, near one hundred and eighty-five metres, or roughly an eighth of a mile. Sixty-one and a quarter stadia is therefore about eleven kilometres, close to seven miles, for the width of a single gate. Luke 24:13 measures the road to Emmaus in the same unit.

Six sunrise points along the eastern horizon, one for each stage of the sun's swing between its summer and its winter extremes, with the sun working back through them as the year turns. 1 Enoch 72:2-7 lays out the same six portals at greater length.

Moed means an appointed time, and it is the word Genesis 1:14 uses when the lights are given for seasons. It is also the word for the appointed feasts at Leviticus 23:2, so the sun's timetable and the calendar of assemblies are named with the same term.

Enoch is presented as taking the measurement himself rather than being handed a figure. The claim is repeated wherever this book gives numbers, and it is the reason the calendar chapters read like a survey report.

Genesis 8:22 describes the year by its working turns, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter. The division into four named seasons that this chapter uses is the Greek one, and it arrives in this literature with the Greek astronomy alongside it.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch is set at the sun's eastern gates and measures them for himself: six gates, each sixty-one stadia and a quarter, through which the sun leaves and to which it returns as the seasons turn and the year closes out.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 14
summaryBullets: And again those men led me away to the western parts, and showed me six great gates open corresponding to the eastern gates, opposite to where the sun sets, according to the number of the days three hundred and sixty-five and A quarter. (14:1).

Thus again it goes down to the western gates, (and) draws away its light, the greatness of its brightness, under the earth; for since the crown of its shining is in heaven with the Lord, and guarded by four hundred angels, while the sun goes round on wheel under the earth, and stands seven great hours in night, and spends half (its course) under the earth, when it comes to the eastern approach in the eighth hour of the night, it brings its lights, and the crown of shining, and the sun flames forth more than fire. (14:2).
crossRefs: Genesis 1:14-19: The fourth day sets the two great lights in the firmament to rule the day and the night and to mark days and years.
Psalm 104:19-20: He appointed the moon for seasons and the sun knows his going down, and when God makes darkness it is night.
Habakkuk 3:11: The sun and moon stand still in their habitation, a line that assumes the lights have a dwelling to stop in.
Joshua 10:12-13: The sun stands still over Gibeon and the moon over the valley of Ajalon, and the sun did not hasten to go down for about a whole day.
1 Enoch 72:33-37: The other Enoch book closes its account of the sun by tracking how day and night trade lengths across the year and totalling the circuit.

translationNotes.term: Three hundred and sixty-five and a quarter
translationNotes.note: The solar year as this chapter fixes it. The quarter day left over is the reason any calendar has to add a day from time to time, and the book explains its own way of handling that when it turns to the moon.

Night was divided into twelve equal parts between sunset and sunrise, so a night hour stretches in winter and shrinks in summer and is rarely sixty minutes. The text has the sun stand seven of those hours under the earth and reach the eastern approach in the eighth.

The book separates the sun's body from its light, leaving the crown of brightness in heaven under guard while the disc itself travels below. That is offered as the reason night is dark. Scripture does not divide the two.

This book puts a number on every angelic duty: two hundred over the stars, three hundred keeping the garden, a hundred kindling the sun, four hundred guarding its crown. Scripture gives no such counts, and the numbering is this book's habit.

The night route the book describes assumes the sun passes beneath a flat earth and comes up on the far side, which is how Egypt and Mesopotamia pictured it. Scripture reports the rising and the setting and says nothing about what lies between.

stories.keyTakeaway: Six western gates match the six in the east, and the year is counted at three hundred and sixty-five days and a quarter. The sun leaves its crown of light in heaven under four hundred guards while it travels seven hours beneath the earth.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 15
summaryBullets: Then the elements of the sun, called Phoenixes and Chalkydri break into song, therefore every bird flutters with its wings, rejoicing at the giver of light, and they broke into song at the command of the Lord. (15:1).

The giver of light comes to give brightness to the whole world, and the morning guard takes shape, which is the rays of the sun, and the sun of the earth goes out, and receives its brightness to light up the whole face of the earth, and they showed me this calculation of the sun's going. (15:2).

And the gates which it enters, these are the great gates of the calculation of the hours of the year; for this reason the sun is a great creation, whose circuit (lasts) twenty-eight years, and begins again from the beginning. (15:3).
crossRefs: Psalm 148:3-10: Sun, moon, stars and every flying bird are called on to praise the LORD, the same chorus this chapter puts at sunrise.
Job 38:7: The morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy when the foundations of the earth were laid.
Psalm 19:1-6: The heavens tell the glory of God without speech or language, and the sun goes out from his chamber and runs his course.
Genesis 1:14-16: The lights are given to divide day from night and to fix signs, seasons, days and years, which is the reckoning these gates are said to keep.
1 Enoch 75:1-3: The other Enoch book assigns leaders to the days that fall outside the reckoned months, and says men go wrong in the count by leaving them out.

translationNotes.note: A guard is a watch, a fixed block of the night with sentries posted. The morning watch is the last one before daylight, and Exodus 14:24 has the LORD look out on the Egyptian host in the morning watch. Here the term is transferred to the first rays of the sun.

The solar cycle. Because the year runs three hundred and sixty-five days and a quarter, a given date falls on the same weekday again only after twenty-eight years, which is seven days multiplied by the four-year leap step. That figure returns later as one half of the great cycle.

The phrase is applied here to the sun and not to God. The book has already said the sun's crown of shining is kept in heaven under guard, so the light it brings at dawn is described as light handed to it rather than light it owns.

translationNotes.term: Every bird flutters with its wings
translationNotes.note: The dawn chorus. Birds in that region begin calling well before the sun clears the horizon, and the book treats the noise as the birds joining the song of the sun's attendants. Mark 13:35 names a whole watch of the night after the same habit in a cock.

translationNotes.term: The calculation of the hours of the year
translationNotes.note: Hours here are not fixed units of sixty minutes. Daylight and darkness were each cut into twelve, so a daylight hour ran long in summer and short in winter, and the gate the sun is using on a given day fixes how long an hour lasts.

stories.keyTakeaway: At dawn the sun's attendant creatures break into song and every bird beats its wings. Enoch is shown the reckoning behind it: the gates count the hours of the year, and the sun's full circuit runs twenty-eight years before it starts over.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 16
summaryBullets: Those men showed me the other course, that of the moon, twelve great gates, crowned from west to east, by which the moon goes in and out of the customary times. (16:1).

It goes in at the first gate to the western places of the sun, by the first gates with (thirty)-one (days) exactly, by the second gates with thirty-one days exactly, by the third with thirty days exactly, by the fourth with thirty days exactly, by the fifth with thirty-one days exactly, by the sixth with thirty-one days exactly, by the seventh with thirty days exactly, by the eighth with thirty-one days perfectly, by the ninth with thirty-one days exactly, by the tenth with thirty days perfectly, by the eleventh with thirty-one days exactly, by the twelfth with twenty-eight days exactly. (16:2).

And it goes through the western gates in the order and number of the eastern, and accomplishes the three hundred and sixty-five and a quarter days of the solar year, while the lunar year has three hundred fifty-four, and there are wanting (to it) twelve days of the solar circle, which are the lunar epacts of the whole year. (16:3).
Thus, too, the great circle contains five hundred and thirty-two years. (16:4).
The quarter (of a day) is omitted for three years, the fourth fulfills it exactly. (16:5).

Therefore they are taken outside of heaven for three years and are not added to the number of days, because they change the time of the years to two new months towards completion, to two others towards diminution. (16:6).

And when the western gates are finished, it returns and goes to the eastern to the lights, and goes thus day and night about the heavenly circles, lower than all circles, swifter than the heavenly winds, and spirits and elements and angels flying; each angel has six wings. (16:7).
It has a sevenfold course in nineteen years. (16:8).
crossRefs: Genesis 1:14-16: The lesser light is set to rule the night, and the lights together are given for signs and for seasons.
Psalm 104:19: He appointed the moon for seasons, the office this chapter works out in figures.
Psalm 81:3: The horn is blown at the new moon at the time appointed for the feast day, so the month was read off the moon.
1 Enoch 73:1-8: The other Enoch book gives the moon her own account, her light, her waxing and the portals she uses.
1 Enoch 78:6-17: The phases are counted out there day by day, with the moon's light growing and shrinking in fourteen parts.

translationNotes.note: Epact means added days, and it names the gap between a lunar year and a solar one. This chapter sets the solar year at three hundred and sixty-five days and a quarter, the lunar year at three hundred and fifty-four, and calls the shortfall twelve days. By those two figures the gap works out at eleven and a quarter.

The great cycle, and it is a multiplication. Nineteen years for the moon's pattern to repeat against the sun, times twenty-eight years for dates to fall on the same weekdays again, gives five hundred and thirty-two. This book names both factors, the twenty-eight in the sun's chapter and the nineteen at the close of this one.

translationNotes.term: A sevenfold course in nineteen years
translationNotes.note: Nineteen solar years come out almost exactly equal to two hundred and thirty-five lunar months. Nineteen years of twelve months is two hundred and twenty-eight, so seven extra months have to be inserted across the cycle to keep the moon in step with the sun. That seven is the sevenfold course.

The twelve figures given for the moon's gates run thirty-one, thirty-one, thirty, thirty, thirty-one, thirty-one, thirty, thirty-one, thirty-one, thirty, thirty-one and twenty-eight, and they add up to three hundred and sixty-five. They are not lunar months, which average about twenty-nine and a half days each.

translationNotes.term: The quarter is omitted for three years
translationNotes.note: The leftover quarter of a day is dropped for three years running and made good in the fourth, which is a leap day by another name. That same step is why the pattern of dates against weekdays takes twenty-eight years to come round.

The moon is placed nearest the earth, below every other light and moving faster than any of them. That is the standard ancient order of the heavens, and this book keeps it when it sets the lights on their circles in the creation account.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch is shown the moon's twelve gates and every month's length, with the arithmetic behind them: a solar year of three hundred and sixty-five days and a quarter, a lunar year of three hundred and fifty-four, a great cycle of five hundred and thirty-two years, and a sevenfold course in nineteen.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 17
summaryBullets: In the midst of the heavens I saw armed soldiers, serving the Lord, with tympana and organs, with incessant voice, with sweet voice, with sweet and incessant (voice) and various singing, which it is impossible to describe, and (which) astonishes every mind, so wonderful and marvellous is the singing of those angels, and I was delighted listening to it. (17:1).
crossRefs: Isaiah 6:2-3: The seraphim stand above the throne calling to one another, Holy, holy, holy, until the posts of the door move at the voice.
Revelation 5:11-12: Ten thousand times ten thousand angels round the throne say with a loud voice that the Lamb is worthy.
Psalm 150:3-5: The praise is listed instrument by instrument: trumpet, psaltery, harp, timbrel, stringed instruments, organs and cymbals.
Luke 2:13-14: A multitude of the heavenly host appears praising God, the one place Scripture lets men hear the armies of heaven sing.
2 Chronicles 5:12-14: Singers and priests with trumpets sound as one, and the glory fills the house so that the priests cannot stand to minister.

translationNotes.note: Tsava means an army, and host of heaven is the standard phrase for God's forces, which is where the title LORD of hosts comes from. Calling these singers soldiers is not a muddle: the same beings are ranked as troops and organised as a choir.

A hand drum, a hoop with a skin stretched over it, struck with the fingers. Exodus 15:20 has Miriam take a timbrel and lead the women out with dances, which is the instrument's ordinary use in a victory song.
Not a keyboard instrument. The Hebrew word that older English renders organ names a wind instrument, most likely a pipe or reed flute, and it turns up as early as Genesis 4:21 paired with the harp.

translationNotes.term: In the midst of the heavens
translationNotes.note: The phrase puts this host between the levels rather than inside one of them, which is why the chapter stands on its own between the fourth heaven and the fifth in the order of the ascent.

Refusing to describe is a fixed move in this kind of vision writing rather than a lapse. Paul does the same at 2 Corinthians 12:4, saying he heard words which a man is not permitted to utter, and this book reaches for it every time it nears the throne.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch sees armed hosts in the middle of the heavens serving the Lord with drums and pipes and unbroken singing, a sound he says cannot be described and that astonishes any mind that takes it in.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 18
summaryBullets: The men took me on to the fifth heaven and placed me, and there I saw many and countless soldiers, called Grigori, of human appearance, and their size (was) greater than that of great giants and their faces withered, and the silence of their mouths perpetual, and their was no service on the fifth heaven, and I said to the men who were with me: (18:1).
Wherefore are these very withered and their faces melancholy, and their mouths silent, and (wherefore) is there no service on this heaven? (18:2).

And they said to me: These are the Grigori, who with their prince Satanail (Satan) rejected the Lord of light, and after them are those who are held in great darkness on the second heaven, and three of them went down on to earth from the Lord's throne, to the place Ermon, and broke through their vows on the shoulder of the hill Ermon and saw the daughters of men how good they are, and took to themselves wives, and befouled the earth with their deeds, who in all times of their age made lawlessness and mixing, and giants are born and marvellous big men and great enmity. (18:3).
And therefore God judged them with great judgment, and they weep for their brethren and they will be punished on the Lord's great day. (18:4).

And I said to the Grigori: I saw your brethren and their works, and their great torments, and I prayed for them, but the Lord has condemned them (to be) under earth till (the existing) heaven and earth shall end for ever. (18:5).
And I said: Wherefore do you wait, brethren, and do not serve before the Lord's face, and have not put your services before the Lord's face, lest you anger your Lord utterly? (18:6).

And they listened to my admonition, and spoke to the four ranks in heaven, and lo! As I stood with those two men four trumpets trumpeted together with great voice, and the Grigori broke into song with one voice, and their voice went up before the Lord pitifully and affectingly. (18:7).
crossRefs: Genesis 6:1-4: The sons of God take wives of the daughters of men, and there were giants in the earth in those days, which is the event this chapter is retelling.
1 Enoch 6:1-6: Two hundred Watchers come down in the days of Jared onto the summit of Mount Hermon and bind themselves by a mutual oath before taking wives.
1 Enoch 7:1-6: They take wives, teach them charms and the cutting of roots, and the giants born to them consume everything men can produce.
Daniel 4:13-17: A watcher and a holy one comes down from heaven and the decree is issued by the word of the watchers, the only place the title stands in Scripture.
Jude 1:6-7: The angels who left their own habitation are held in everlasting chains under darkness, set beside Sodom and Gomorrha going after strange flesh.

translationNotes.note: Grigori is the Slavonic form of the Greek egregoroi, the wakeful ones, or watchers. The Greek renders the Aramaic irin, and Daniel 4:13 is the one place in Scripture the title appears, where a watcher and a holy one comes down from heaven.

Mount Hermon, the highest mountain in the region at about nine thousand two hundred feet, standing at the southern end of the Anti-Lebanon range and marking the northern limit of the land Israel took, as Deuteronomy 3:8-9 sets it out. 1 Enoch 6:6 says the Watchers came down on its summit and swore there.

Satan in Hebrew means the adversary or the accuser, and it works as a title before it works as a name; at Job 1:6 and Zechariah 3:1 the accuser stands among others in a formal setting. The Slavonic ending il matches the el that closes Michael, Gabriel and Raphael.

The Hebrew word at Genesis 6:4 is nephilim, which the Greek Septuagint renders gigantes, the source of the English giants. Numbers 13:33 uses the same word for what the spies reported seeing in Canaan.

The oath is the hinge of the story. 1 Enoch 6:4-5 has the group bind itself by mutual curses first, so that no one could withdraw once they had begun, and this book reports the same broken oath without repeating the scene.

This book says three of the Grigori went down to Ermon. 1 Enoch 6:6 counts two hundred descending there, and Genesis 6:2 gives no number at all. Each account states its own figure and none of them harmonises the others.

stories.keyTakeaway: In the fifth heaven Enoch finds the Grigori, silent and withered, who rejected the Lord along with their prince Satanail. Three went down to Mount Ermon, broke their vows, took wives among the daughters of men and fathered giants. Enoch urges the rest back to their service, and they sing.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 19
summaryBullets: And from there those men took me and bore me up on to the sixth heaven, and there I saw seven bands of angels, very bright and very glorious, and their faces shining more than the sun's shining, glistening, and there is no difference in their faces, or behaviour, or manner of dress; and these make the orders, and learn the goings of the stars, and the alteration of the moon, or revolution of the sun, and the good government of the world. (19:1).
And when they see evildoing they make commandments and instruction, and sweet and loud singing, and all (songs) of praise. (19:2).

These are the archangels who are above angels, measure all life in heaven and on earth, and the angels who are (appointed) over seasons and years, the angels who are over rivers and sea, and who are over the fruits of the earth, and the angels who are over every grass, giving food to all, to every living thing, and the angels who write all the souls of men, and all their deeds, and their lives before the Lord's face; in their midst are six Phoenixes and six Cherubim and six six-winged ones continually with one voice singing one voice, and it is not possible to describe their singing, and they rejoice before the Lord at his footstool. (19:3).
crossRefs: Daniel 7:10: A thousand thousands minister before the throne, the judgment is set, and the books are opened.
Malachi 3:16: A book of remembrance is written before the LORD for those who feared him and thought upon his name.
Revelation 20:12: The dead stand before God, the books are opened, and they are judged out of the things written in them.
Psalm 104:14-15: He makes grass grow for the cattle and herb for man, bringing bread, wine and oil out of the earth.
1 Enoch 20:1-8: The other Enoch book names the holy angels who watch and gives each one a charge, over the world, over the spirits of men, over the stars and over paradise.

translationNotes.note: The word means chief angel and turns up twice in the New Testament, at 1 Thessalonians 4:16 and at Jude 1:9, where Michael carries the title. Scripture names only Michael and Gabriel among the high ranks; the departments listed in this chapter come from this book.

The seven bands are described as identical in face, behaviour and dress, which marks them as one rank rather than as individuals with names. It is the exact opposite of the Grigori one heaven below, whose withered faces and silence set each of them apart.

translationNotes.term: The angels who write all the souls of men
translationNotes.note: A recording angel. Scripture keeps the record in God's own hand: Malachi 3:16 has a book of remembrance written before the LORD, and Psalm 56:8 puts a man's tears in God's book. The clerks are supplied by this book.

translationNotes.term: Angels who are over every grass
translationNotes.note: Assigning an angel to each class of created thing, down to individual plants, belongs to this book. Psalm 104:14 has God himself causing the grass to grow for the cattle, with nobody standing in between.

translationNotes.term: The good government of the world
translationNotes.note: The phrase covers the ordered running of creation, what older English calls providence. This chapter hands the daily administration of it to ranked angels and then names the departments one by one, seasons, rivers, sea, fruit, grass and the record of souls.

Three groups of six, the third being the six-winged ones, that is the seraphim of Isaiah 6:2. Scripture stations cherubim and seraphim at the throne but never counts them, and the phoenix does not appear in Scripture at all.

stories.keyTakeaway: The sixth heaven holds seven identical bands of shining angels who keep the courses of the stars, the moon and the sun and the government of the world. Others are set over seasons, rivers, crops and grass, and some write down every human soul and deed.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 20
summaryBullets: And those two men lifted me up from there on to the seventh heaven, and I saw there a very great light, and fiery troops of great archangels, incorporeal forces, and dominions, orders and governments, Cherubim and seraphim, thrones and many-eyed ones, nine regiments, the Ioanit stations of light, and I became afraid, and began to tremble with great terror, and those men took me, and led me after them, and said to me: (20:1).
Have courage, Enoch, do not fear, and showed me the Lord from afar, sitting on His very high throne. For what is there on the tenth heaven, since the Lord dwells there? (20:2).
On the tenth heaven is God, in the Hebrew tongue he is called Aravat. (20:3).

And all the heavenly troops would come and stand on the ten steps according to their rank, and would bow down to the Lord, and would again go to their places in joy and felicity, singing songs in the boundless light with small and tender voices, gloriously serving him. (20:4).
crossRefs: Isaiah 6:1-4: The prophet sees the Lord high and lifted up on a throne, with seraphim above it and the house filling with smoke.
Colossians 1:16: All things were created by him and for him, whether thrones or dominions or principalities or powers, the ranks this chapter lists in order.
Ezekiel 1:15-21: The wheels beside the living creatures have rims full of eyes all round, which is the many-eyed order named here.
Psalm 68:4: God is praised as the one who rides upon the aravot, the Hebrew word this chapter gives as the name of the tenth heaven.
Ephesians 1:21: Christ is set far above all principality and power and might and dominion, and above every name that is named.

translationNotes.note: The Hebrew word means clouds or high places, and Psalm 68:4 uses it of the one who rides upon the aravot. The Babylonian Talmud, in tractate Chagigah, lists seven heavens and gives Aravot as the name of the highest. This book keeps the name and puts it on a tenth.

The chapter lists the ranks of heaven in order and counts nine of them. Scripture names cherubim, seraphim, archangels, thrones, dominions, principalities and powers in scattered places but never arranges them in a numbered hierarchy. The count belongs to this book.

The translator left the word standing as it is in the Slavonic. It has no traceable Hebrew or Greek original, and the text says nothing about it beyond calling them stations of light. Guessing at a meaning would be inventing one.

Ezekiel 1:18 describes the wheels beside the living creatures with rims full of eyes all round, and Revelation 4:6-8 gives the four living creatures eyes before and behind. This book turns the description into a rank name of its own, listed beside thrones and cherubim.

The troops bow on ten steps according to rank, one step for each heaven in this book's scheme. Scripture describes ranks around the throne but no stairway, and the ten-level arrangement is the framework of this book rather than a detail inside it.

translationNotes.term: Have courage, Enoch, do not fear
translationNotes.note: The line appears four times in the book, at every point where Enoch is overcome. It is also the standard opening when a heavenly being speaks to a man in Scripture, as at Daniel 10:12 and Luke 1:13, where the first word out is Fear not.

stories.keyTakeaway: The seventh heaven is full of light and ranked hosts: archangels, dominions, thrones, cherubim, seraphim and many-eyed ones in nine regiments. Enoch trembles, is told not to fear, and sees the Lord far off on his throne. God on the tenth heaven is named Aravat.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 21
summaryBullets: And the Cherubim and seraphim standing about the throne, the six-winged and many-eyed ones do not depart, standing before the Lord's face doing his will, and cover his whole throne, singing with gentle voice before the Lord's face: Holy, holy, holy, Lord Ruler of Sabaoth, heavens and earth are full of Your glory. (21:1).
When I saw all these things, those men said to me: Enoch, thus far is it commanded us to journey with you, and those men went away from me and thereupon I saw them not. (21:2).
And I remained alone at the end of the seventh heaven and became afraid, and fell on my face and said to myself: Woe is me, what has befallen me? (21:3).
And the Lord sent one of his glorious ones, the archangel Gabriel, and (he) said to me: Have courage, Enoch, do not fear, arise before the Lord's face into eternity, arise, come with me. (21:4).

And I answered him, and said in myself: My Lord, my soul is departed from me, from terror and trembling, and I called to the men who led me up to this place, on them I relied, and (it is) with them I go before the Lord's face. (21:5).
And Gabriel caught me up, as a leaf caught up by the wind, and placed me before the Lord's face. (21:6).

And I saw the eighth heaven, which is called in the Hebrew tongue Muzaloth, changer of the seasons, of drought, and of wet, and of the twelve constellations of the circle of the firmament, which are above the seventh heaven. (21:7).
And I saw the ninth heaven, which is called in Hebrew Kuchavim, where are the heavenly homes of the twelve constellations of the circle of the firmament. (21:8).
crossRefs: Isaiah 6:1-3: The seraphim above the throne cry Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts, and the whole earth is full of his glory.
Revelation 4:8: The four living creatures rest neither day nor night, saying Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, which was and is and is to come.
Daniel 8:15-18: Gabriel is sent to explain a vision, the prophet falls on his face in a deep sleep, and Gabriel sets him upright on his feet.
Luke 1:19: The angel answers, I am Gabriel, that stand in the presence of God, and am sent to speak unto thee.
2 Kings 23:5: Josiah puts down the priests who burned incense to the mazzalot, the Hebrew word this chapter uses as the name of the eighth heaven.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ (qadosh qadosh qadosh)
translationNotes.note: Hebrew has no separate words for more and most, so it raises a term by repeating it. Saying holy three times is the strongest form the language allows, and Isaiah 6:3 and Revelation 4:8 both use it at the throne.
The word means armies or hosts. Greek did not translate it but carried the Hebrew sound across whole, which is why Romans 9:29 and James 5:4 read Lord of Sabaoth in English instead of Lord of hosts.

The Hebrew word for the constellations of the zodiac. 2 Kings 23:5 uses it of the star signs that priests in Judah burned incense to before Josiah put them down. This book turns the word into the name of the eighth heaven, the level that changes seasons and weather.

The plain Hebrew plural for stars. The book uses it as the name of the ninth heaven and says the twelve constellations keep their homes there, so the ninth is where the stars live and the eighth is the circle they travel.

translationNotes.term: As a leaf caught up by the wind
translationNotes.note: Being carried bodily is how these journeys work. Ezekiel 8:3 has the spirit lift the prophet between the earth and the heaven, and Acts 8:39 has the Spirit catch Philip away from the road. The leaf is this book's own image for it.

The name means man of God, or God is my strength. Gabriel appears at Daniel 8:16 and Daniel 9:21 to explain visions and at Luke 1:19 to announce a birth. His work in Scripture is always to interpret or announce, which is what he does here.

stories.keyTakeaway: The cherubim and seraphim sing Holy, holy, holy at the throne. Enoch's two guides leave him and he is alone and terrified until Gabriel comes and carries him up like a leaf in the wind, past the eighth heaven Muzaloth and the ninth, Kuchavim.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 22
summaryBullets: On the tenth heaven, (which is called) Aravoth, I saw the appearance of the Lord's face, like iron made to glow in fire, and brought out, emitting sparks, and it burns. (22:1).
Thus (in a moment of eternity) I saw the Lord's face, but the Lord's face is ineffable, marvellous and very awful, and very, very terrible. (22:2).

And who am I to tell of the Lord's unspeakable being, and of his very wonderful face? And I cannot tell the quantity of his many instructions, and various voices, the Lord's throne (is) very great and not made with hands, nor the quantity of those standing round him, troops of Cherubim and seraphim, nor their incessant singing, nor his immutable beauty, and who shall tell of the ineffable greatness of his glory. (22:3).
And I fell prone and bowed down to the Lord, and the Lord with his lips said to me: (22:4).
Have courage, Enoch, do not fear, arise and stand before my face into eternity. (22:5).
And the archistratege Michael lifted me up, and led me to before the Lord's face. (22:6).
And the Lord said to his servants tempting them: Let Enoch stand before my face into eternity, and the glorious ones bowed down to the Lord, and said: Let Enoch go according to Your word. (22:7).
And the Lord said to Michael: Go and take Enoch from out (of) his earthly garments, and anoint him with my sweet ointment, and put him into the garments of My glory. (22:8).

And Michael did thus, as the Lord told him. He anointed me, and dressed me, and the appearance of that ointment is more than the great light, and his ointment is like sweet dew, and its smell mild, shining like the sun's ray, and I looked at myself, and (I) was like (transfigured) one of his glorious ones. (22:9).

And the Lord summoned one of his archangels by name Pravuil, whose knowledge was quicker in wisdom than the other archangels, who wrote all the deeds of the Lord; and the Lord said to Pravuil: Bring out the books from my store-houses, and a reed of quick-writing, and give (it) to Enoch, and deliver to him the choice and comforting books out of your hand. (22:10).
crossRefs: Exodus 29:5-7: Aaron is dressed in the priestly garments and then the anointing oil is poured on his head, the same order of vesting and anointing used here.
Zechariah 3:3-5: Joshua the high priest stands in filthy garments, they are taken off him, and he is clothed with change of raiment and a clean mitre.
Ezekiel 1:26-28: Above the firmament is a throne, and on it a likeness with the appearance of fire and a brightness all round it.
Daniel 10:5-6: The man clothed in linen has a face like lightning, eyes like lamps of fire, and arms and feet like polished brass.
Genesis 5:24: Enoch walked with God and was not, for God took him, the one verse this whole scene is expanding.

translationNotes.note: The word means commander-in-chief of an army. The Greek Septuagint uses it at Joshua 5:14 for the captain of the host of the LORD who meets Joshua with a drawn sword. Giving Michael the title matches Daniel 12:1, which calls him the great prince who stands for the people.

translationNotes.term: Anoint him with my sweet ointment
translationNotes.note: The holy anointing oil was made to a fixed recipe at Exodus 30:22-25 out of myrrh, sweet cinnamon, sweet calamus, cassia and olive oil, and Exodus 30:32-33 makes copying it or putting it on an outsider a capital matter. Its purpose was to set a man apart for office.

Changing clothes marks a change of standing rather than of dress. Zechariah 3:3-5 strips the filthy garments off the high priest and gives him clean ones as the sign that his guilt has been taken away, and this chapter runs the same procedure on Enoch.

An archangel named only in this book, described as quicker in wisdom than the rest and keeper of the record of the Lord's deeds. Scripture names no heavenly librarian, and 1 Enoch 12:4 gives the title of scribe to Enoch himself rather than to an angel.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עֵט סוֹפֵר מָהִיר (et sofer mahir)
translationNotes.note: A pen cut from river reed and split at the tip was the ordinary writing tool. Psalm 45:1 uses nearly the same phrase, the pen of a ready writer, meaning a scribe who can take dictation at speed, which is exactly the post Enoch is handed.

translationNotes.term: Like iron made to glow in fire
translationNotes.note: Worked iron runs from red through orange to white as it heats and throws sparks when it is struck or drawn. The comparison is to a working forge, a sight everyone hearing it knew. Ezekiel 1:27 reaches for the colour of glowing metal to describe the same vision.

stories.keyTakeaway: On the tenth heaven Enoch sees the Lord's face like iron glowing in fire and falls flat. Michael takes him out of his earthly garments, anoints him with the ointment of glory and dresses him in the garments of glory, and he looks like one of the glorious ones.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 23
summaryBullets: And he was telling me all the works of heaven, earth and sea, and all the elements, their passages and goings, and the thunderings of the thunders, the sun and moon, the goings and changes of the stars, the seasons, years, days, and hours, the risings of the wind, the numbers of the angels, and the formation of their songs, and all human things, the tongue of every human song and life, the commandments, instructions, and sweet-voiced singings, and all things that it is fitting to learn. (23:1).

And Pravuil told me: All the things that I have told you, we have written. Sit and write all the souls of mankind, however many of them are born, and the places prepared for them to eternity; for all souls are prepared to eternity, before the formation of the world. (23:2).
And all double thirty days and thirty nights, and I wrote out all things exactly, and wrote three hundred and sixty-six books. (23:3).
crossRefs: Psalm 139:16: In God's book all the days were written before there were any of them, the same idea of a record made before the life is lived.
Jeremiah 1:5: Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee, and before thou camest out of the womb I sanctified thee.
2 Esdras 4:35-37: The souls of the righteous ask in their chambers how long they must wait, and are told the times are weighed and the number measured.
Exodus 24:18: Moses goes into the cloud on the mountain and stays forty days and forty nights, the nearest parallel to a man kept above for a counted span.
1 Enoch 33:3-4: Uriel shows Enoch the portals of the stars and their names, and Enoch writes them down as they are shown to him.

translationNotes.note: The number stands one above the three hundred and sixty-five years Genesis 5:23 gives Enoch and one above the days this book assigns the solar year. It is stated twice, here and in the closing chapter, so the figure is meant.

A fixed span of writing, counted the way Scripture counts Moses on the mountain at Exodus 24:18 and Exodus 34:28, forty days and forty nights without bread or water. The pattern of a set period alone with God is the same; the number is not.

translationNotes.term: All souls are prepared to eternity
translationNotes.note: The book states that every soul exists in God's plan before the world is made and that its place is already assigned. Scripture speaks of God knowing a man before birth at Jeremiah 1:5 and of the days written in his book at Psalm 139:16. The stock of prepared souls is this book's way of putting it.

translationNotes.term: The tongue of every human song
translationNotes.note: Languages are treated as a subject to be catalogued and written down. Genesis 11:1-9 accounts for their number at Babel, and Acts 2:9-11 lists about fifteen peoples by their speech in a single sentence, which is the kind of inventory this line has in view.

A book at this date is a roll and not bound pages: sheets of papyrus glued end to end, wound on a rod and written in columns. Jeremiah 36:23 shows what that means physically, when the king cuts the roll up with a penknife and burns it a few columns at a time.

stories.keyTakeaway: Pravuil dictates the workings of heaven, earth and sea, the courses of the lights, the count of the angels and the speech of every people. Enoch writes for thirty days and thirty nights and produces three hundred and sixty-six books.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 24
summaryBullets: And the Lord summoned me, and said to me: Enoch, sit down on my left with Gabriel. (24:1).
