And I bowed down to the Lord, and the Lord spoke to me: Enoch, beloved, all (that) you see, all things that are standing finished I tell to you even before the very beginning, all that I created from non-being, and visible (physical) things from invisible (spiritual). (24:2).

Hear, Enoch, and take in these my words, for not to My angels have I told my secret, and I have not told them their rise, nor my endless realm, nor have they understood my creating, which I tell you to-day. (24:3).
For before all things were visible (physical), I alone used to go about in the invisible (spiritual) things, like the sun from east to west, and from west to east. (24:4).

But even the sun has peace in itself, while I found no peace, because I was creating all things, and I conceived the thought of placing foundations, and of creating visible (physical) creation. (24:5).
crossRefs: Hebrews 11:3: The worlds were framed by the word of God, so that the things which are seen were not made of things which appear.
Genesis 1:1-2: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth, and the earth was without form and void, the account this chapter runs behind.
Isaiah 40:13-14: Who has directed the Spirit of the LORD, or been his counsellor, or taught him in the path of judgment.
Deuteronomy 29:29: The secret things belong to the LORD our God, and the things revealed belong to us and to our children for ever.
1 Peter 1:12: The things now announced are things the angels desire to look into, so Scripture also has matters not first told to angels.

translationNotes.note: Seating is rank. The right hand is the place of highest honour, which is why Psalm 110:1 says sit thou at my right hand, and here Gabriel and Enoch are set on the left. Scripture never seats a man at God's own throne; this book does.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ἐξ οὐκ ὄντων (ex ouk onton)
translationNotes.note: Out of what does not exist. 2 Maccabees 7:28 uses that Greek phrase when a mother tells her son to look at heaven and earth and understand that God made them out of things that were not, and Hebrews 11:3 says the visible was not made out of what appears.

The words in brackets through these chapters are the translator's gloss and not part of the text. The Slavonic pair means seen and unseen, which is the same distinction Colossians 1:16 draws when it says all things visible and invisible were created by him.

The line says God had no rest of his own while the work was going on. Genesis 2:2 has him rest on the seventh day once the work was finished, and Exodus 20:11 makes that rest the ground of the sabbath command. This book adds what the working days were like.

translationNotes.term: Not to My angels have I told my secret
translationNotes.note: The claim is that Enoch is being told what the angels never were, including how they themselves came to be. Deuteronomy 29:29 keeps secret things with God, and 1 Peter 1:12 says angels desire to look into what has now been announced to men.

stories.keyTakeaway: God seats Enoch at his left hand with Gabriel and tells him what he told no angel: that he made everything out of non-being, brought the visible out of the invisible, and had no rest of his own while he was creating.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 25
summaryBullets: I commanded in the very lowest (parts), that visible (physical) things should come down from invisible (spiritual), and Adoil came down very great, and I beheld him, and lo! He had a belly of great light. (25:1).
And I said to him: Become undone, Adoil, and let the visible (physical) (come) out of you. (25:2).

And he came undone, and a great light came out. And I (was) in the midst of the great light, and as there is born light from light, there came forth a great age, and showed all creation, which I had thought to create. (25:3).
And I saw that (it was) good. (25:4).
And I placed for myself a throne, and took my seat on it, and said to the light: Go from there up higher and fix yourself high above the throne, and be A foundation to the highest things. (25:5).
And above the light there is nothing else, and then I bent up and looked up from my throne. (25:6).
crossRefs: Genesis 1:3-4: God said, Let there be light, and there was light, and God saw the light that it was good and divided it from the darkness.
Job 38:4-7: God asks who laid the foundations of the earth, who stretched the line upon it, and on what its foundations were fastened.
Proverbs 8:27-29: Wisdom is present when he prepares the heavens, sets a compass on the face of the depth, and appoints the foundations of the earth.
Psalm 104:2: He covers himself with light as with a garment and stretches out the heavens like a curtain.
Isaiah 66:1: Heaven is my throne and the earth is my footstool, which is the language Scripture uses of God's seat and its foundation.

translationNotes.note: A being named only in this book, whose single act is to burst open and release the light the visible age is made from. Nothing in Scripture corresponds to him. The ending il matches the el that closes Hebrew angel names like Michael and Gabriel, but the rest of the name cannot be traced to any known word.

The verb means to come apart or be unfastened, and it is used twice in these chapters, here of Adoil and again of Archas. Creation in this account proceeds by two great beings being opened up, where Genesis 1:3 has it proceed by a spoken command.

Aion means an age, a stretch of time, and by extension the world that fills it. English versions render it world in places like Matthew 13:39, which is why one word can carry a period and a created order at once. Here it names what came out of Adoil.

translationNotes.term: I saw that it was good
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים כִּי־טוֹב (vayyar Elohim ki tov)
translationNotes.note: This is the refrain of Genesis 1, repeated at each stage of the work there. The book keeps the sentence word for word and attaches it to its own account of what happened before the first day began.

translationNotes.term: A foundation to the highest things
translationNotes.note: Foundation language runs through this chapter and the next: light fixed above as the base of the upper world, darkness fixed below as the base of the lower. Job 38:4-6 uses the same building vocabulary, with foundations, a measuring line and a corner stone.

stories.keyTakeaway: God tells Enoch how the visible began. A great being called Adoil comes down carrying light in his belly, is told to come undone, and the light that bursts out of him becomes the age and is fixed above the throne as the foundation of everything high.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 26
summaryBullets: And I summoned the very lowest a second time, and said: Let Archas come forth hard, and he came forth hard from the invisible (spiritual). (26:1).
And Archas came forth, hard, heavy, and very red. (26:2).

And I said: Be opened, Archas, and let there be born from you, and he came undone, an age came forth, very great and very dark, bearing the creation of all lower things, and I saw that (it was) good and said to him: (26:3).

Go from there down below, and make yourself firm, and be a foundation for the lower things, and it happened and he went down and fixed himself, and became the foundation for the lower things, and below the darkness there is nothing else. (26:4).
crossRefs: Genesis 1:2: The earth was without form and void, and darkness was upon the face of the deep, which is the state this chapter accounts for.
Job 26:7: He stretches out the north over the empty place and hangs the earth upon nothing.
Job 38:4-6: God asks who laid the foundations of the earth, on what they were fastened, and who laid its corner stone.
Psalm 24:2: He has founded the earth upon the seas and established it upon the floods.
Isaiah 45:7: I form the light and create darkness, says the LORD, so both are traced to one maker.

translationNotes.note: A being named only in this book and the counterpart of Adoil. Where Adoil carries light and goes up, Archas is hard, heavy and red and goes down to be the base of the lower world. Nothing in Scripture corresponds to him and the name cannot be traced to a known word.

Tehom is the deep, the mass of water under and around the world, and it is the word at Genesis 1:2 for what the darkness lay on. Genesis 7:11 has the fountains of the great deep broken up when the flood begins, so the deep is treated as a real reservoir underneath.

Red is the one property given for the substance of the lower creation. Hebrew already ties red to earth by sound and root: adamah is the ground, adom is red, and adam is the man taken out of the ground at Genesis 2:7.

The same word used of what came out of Adoil, so this account has two ages, one of light above and one of darkness below, each becoming a foundation. The pairing is exact and deliberate, and it has no counterpart in Genesis.

translationNotes.term: Below the darkness there is nothing else
translationNotes.note: The sentence closes the frame: light above with nothing beyond it, darkness below with nothing beneath it. Those are the outer limits of the created order in this book, and everything else is built in the space between them.

stories.keyTakeaway: God summons a second being, Archas, hard and heavy and red, and orders him opened. Out of him comes a dark age carrying the whole lower creation, and he is fixed underneath as the foundation of everything below.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 27
summaryBullets: And I commanded that there should be taken from light and darkness, and I said: Be thick, and it became thus, and I spread it out with the light, and it became water, and I spread it out over the darkness, below the light, and then I made firm the waters, that is to say the bottomless, and I made foundation of light around the water, and created seven circles from inside, and imaged (the water) like crystal wet and dry, that is to say like glass, (and) the circumcession of the waters and the other elements, and I showed each one of them its road, and the seven stars each one of them in its heaven, that they go thus, and I saw that it was good. (27:1).

And I separated between light and between darkness, that is to say in the midst of the water here and there, and I said to the light, that it should be the day, and to the darkness, that it should be the night, and there was evening and there was morning the first day. (27:2).
crossRefs: Genesis 1:3-5: God divides the light from the darkness, calls them day and night, and the evening and the morning are the first day.
Genesis 1:6-8: God makes a firmament in the midst of the waters to divide the waters from the waters, and calls the firmament heaven.
Revelation 4:6: Before the throne is a sea of glass like unto crystal, the same comparison this chapter makes for the water.
Ezekiel 1:22: The firmament stretched over the heads of the living creatures has the colour of the terrible crystal.
Proverbs 8:27: When he prepared the heavens wisdom was there, and when he set a compass upon the face of the depth.

translationNotes.note: The seven spheres of the ancient sky, one for each light that moves against the fixed background: the moon, Mercury, Venus, the sun, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn. Everything else was held to belong to the outer sphere. This is the framework the book uses when it names the planets in the creation account.

Star here means any moving light, which is exactly what planet means in Greek: planetes, a wanderer, something that shifts position against the fixed stars. The five planets visible without a telescope, plus the sun and the moon, make seven.

translationNotes.term: Like crystal wet and dry, that is to say like glass
translationNotes.note: Glass in this period was expensive and usually cloudy, so clear glass was a luxury and a natural image for something perfectly transparent. Revelation 4:6 puts a sea of glass like crystal before the throne and Ezekiel 1:22 gives the firmament the colour of terrible crystal.
Abyssos means without a bottom, and the Greek Septuagint uses it for the Hebrew tehom, the deep of Genesis 1:2. The New Testament keeps it as a place name, the bottomless pit at Revelation 9:1-2.

The day is counted from evening to evening rather than from midnight. That is why Leviticus 23:32 fixes the Day of Atonement from evening unto evening, and why a sabbath begins at sundown and not at dawn.

stories.keyTakeaway: God tells how he took from light and darkness and made water, set seven circles inside it with a star in each, gave every element its road, then divided light from darkness so the first day closed with an evening and a morning.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 28
summaryBullets: And then I made firm the heavenly circle, and (made) that the lower water which is under heaven collect itself together, into one whole, and that the chaos become dry, and it became so. (28:1).

Out of the waves I created rock hard and big, and from the rock I piled up the dry, and the dry I called earth, and the midst of the earth I called abyss, that is to say the bottomless, I collected the sea in one place and bound it together with a yoke. (28:2).
And I said to the sea: Behold I give you (your) eternal limits, and you shalt not break loose from your component parts. (28:3).
Thus I made fast the firmament. This day I called me the first-created [Sunday]. (28:4).
crossRefs: Genesis 1:9-10: The waters under heaven are gathered into one place, the dry land appears, and God calls the dry land earth and the gathered waters seas.
Job 38:8-11: The sea is shut up with doors and a bar and told, Hitherto shalt thou come, but no further, and here shall thy proud waves be stayed.
Jeremiah 5:22: God has set the sand as the bound of the sea by a perpetual decree, and though the waves toss they cannot pass over it.
Psalm 104:5-9: He laid the foundations of the earth and set a bound the waters may not pass, so that they never return to cover the earth.
Proverbs 8:29: He gave to the sea his decree, that the waters should not pass his commandment.

translationNotes.term: Bound it together with a yoke
translationNotes.note: A yoke is the timber harness locked across the necks of a pair of oxen so they can pull only where the driver steers. Using it of the sea makes the shoreline a harness rather than a wall, which is the same idea as the doors and the bar at Job 38:10.

translationNotes.term: The abyss in the midst of the earth
translationNotes.note: The book puts the bottomless in the middle of the earth rather than outside it. Genesis 7:11 has the fountains of the great deep break up from below, and Jonah 2:5-6 has a man go down to the bottoms of the mountains with the deep closing over him.
The Greek word means a gap or a yawning open space, not disorder; the modern sense of chaos as confusion came much later. Here it names the watery gap that the dry land was piled up out of.

A choq is a decree cut into something, a fixed statute. Jeremiah 5:22 uses it of the sand set as the sea's boundary by perpetual decree, so a coastline is described as a law rather than as an accident of terrain.

The day names in square brackets through these chapters are the translator's additions, not the text. The book matches its days of creation to days of the week and calls this one the first-created. Genesis numbers its days and never names any of them.

stories.keyTakeaway: God gathers the lower water into one body, raises rock out of the waves to pile up dry land, binds the sea inside limits it cannot break, and names this day the first-created.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 29
summaryBullets: And for all the heavenly troops I imaged the image and essence of fire, and my eye looked at the very hard, firm rock, and from the gleam of my eye the lightning received its wonderful nature, (which) is both fire in water and water in fire, and one does not put out the other, nor does the one dry up the other, therefore the lightning is brighter than the sun, softer than water and firmer than hard rock. (29:1).

And from the rock I cut off a great fire, and from the fire I created the orders of the incorporeal ten troops of angels, and their weapons are fiery and their raiment a burning flame, and I commanded that each one should stand in his order. (29:2).

And one from out the order of angels, having turned away with the order that was under him, conceived an impossible thought, to place his throne higher than the clouds above the earth, that he might become equal in rank to my power. (29:3).
And I threw him out from the height with his angels, and he was flying in the air continuously above the bottomless. (29:4).
crossRefs: Isaiah 14:12-15: The taunt over the king of Babylon quotes his boast to raise his throne above the stars of God and be like the Most High, and answers that he is brought down to the pit.
Ezekiel 28:12-17: The lament over the king of Tyre sets him in Eden covered in precious stones until his heart is lifted up by his own beauty and he is cast to the ground.
Luke 10:18: Jesus says, I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven.
Revelation 12:7-9: Michael and his angels fight the dragon and his angels, and the dragon is cast out into the earth with his angels after him.
Psalm 104:4: He makes his angels spirits and his ministers a flaming fire, which is the material this chapter says they were made from.

translationNotes.note: The book counts ten orders of angels cut out of fire, matching its ten heavens. Scripture names cherubim, seraphim, thrones, dominions, principalities and powers in different places and never totals the list. The ten is this book's arrangement.

translationNotes.term: His throne higher than the clouds
translationNotes.note: Isaiah 14:13-14 puts almost this same sentence in the mouth of the king of Babylon: I will ascend above the heights of the clouds, I will be like the most High. The book uses that wording for the angel who fell.

translationNotes.term: Fire in water and water in fire
translationNotes.note: This is a description of lightning, and the puzzle it is answering is real: fire falls with the rain and neither one cancels the other. Exodus 9:24 reports the same combination during the plague of hail, fire mingled with the hail.

Without a body. The word is a technical term out of Greek philosophy, taken over to say that angels have no material substance, and it sits oddly beside this chapter's claim that they were cut out of a rock and a fire. The book states both.

The fallen commander is not put into the abyss in this chapter but left flying in the air above it. Ephesians 2:2 calls the adversary the prince of the power of the air, while Jude 1:6 has angels held in chains under darkness. This book keeps the leader airborne.

stories.keyTakeaway: God makes the heavenly armies out of fire cut from rock, ten orders of them in fiery armour. One commander takes the division under him and plans to set his throne above the clouds and rank with God, and is thrown out to fly above the bottomless.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 30
summaryBullets: On the third day I commanded the earth to make grow great and fruitful trees, and hills, and seed to sow, and I planted Paradise, and enclosed it, and placed as armed (guardians) flaming angels, and thus I created renewal. (30:1).
Then came evening, and came morning the fourth day. (30:2).
[Wednesday]. On the fourth day I commanded that there should be great lights on the heavenly circles. (30:3).

On the first uppermost circle I placed the stars, Kruno, and on the second Aphrodit, on the third Aris, on the fifth Zoues, on the sixth Ermis, on the seventh lesser the moon, and adorned it with the lesser stars. (30:4).
And on the lower I placed the sun for the illumination of day, and the moon and stars for the illumination of night. (30:5).

The sun that it should go according to each constellation, twelve, and I appointed the succession of the months and their names and lives, their thunderings, and their hour-markings, how they should succeed. (30:6).
Then evening came and morning came the fifth day. (30:7).

[Thursday]. On the fifth day I commanded the sea, that it should bring forth fishes, and feathered birds of many varieties, and all animals creeping over the earth, going forth over the earth on four legs, and soaring in the air, male sex and female, and every soul breathing the spirit of life. (30:8).
And there came evening, and there came morning the sixth day. (30:9).

[Friday]. On the sixth day I commanded my wisdom to create man from seven consistencies: one, his flesh from the earth; two, his blood from the dew; three, his eyes from the sun; four, his bones from stone; five, his intelligence from the swiftness of the angels and from cloud; six, his veins and his hair from the grass of the earth; seven, his soul from my breath and from the wind. (30:10).

And I gave him seven natures: to the flesh hearing, the eyes for sight, to the soul smell, the veins for touch, the blood for taste, the bones for endurance, to the intelligence sweetness [enjoyment]. (30:11).

I conceived a cunning saying to say, I created man from invisible (spiritual) and from visible (physical) nature, of both are his death and life and image, he knows speech like some created thing, small in greatness and again great in smallness, and I placed him on earth, a second angel, honourable, great and glorious, and I appointed him as ruler to rule on earth and to have my wisdom, and there was none like him of earth of all my existing creatures. (30:12).

And I appointed him a name, from the four component parts, from east, from west, from south, from north, and I appointed for him four special stars, and I called his name Adam, and showed him the two ways, the light and the darkness, and I told him: (30:13).
This is good, and that bad, that I should learn whether he has love towards me, or hatred, that it be clear which in his race love me. (30:14).
For I have seen his nature, but he has not seen his own nature, therefore (through) not seeing he will sin worse, and I said After sin (what is there) but death? (30:15).

And I put sleep into him and he fell asleep. And I took from him A rib, and created him a wife, that death should come to him by his wife, and I took his last word and called her name mother, that is to say, Eva (Eve). (30:16).
crossRefs: Genesis 1:11-13: The earth brings forth grass, herb yielding seed and fruit trees, and the evening and the morning are the third day.
Genesis 1:14-19: God sets the lights in the firmament, the greater to rule the day and the lesser the night, and he makes the stars also.
Genesis 2:7: The LORD God forms man of the dust of the ground and breathes into his nostrils the breath of life, and man becomes a living soul.
Genesis 2:21-23: A deep sleep falls on Adam, God takes one of his ribs and makes a woman, and Adam calls her bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh.
Deuteronomy 30:15-19: Life and good, death and evil are set before the people and they are told to choose life, the two ways this chapter says Adam was shown.

translationNotes.original: Greek: Κρόνος, Ἀφροδίτη, Ἄρης, Ζεύς, Ἑρμῆς (Kronos, Aphrodite, Ares, Zeus, Hermes)
translationNotes.note: The planets under the names of the Greek gods: Kronos is Saturn, Aphrodite is Venus, Ares is Mars, Zeus is Jupiter, Hermes is Mercury, and the Roman equivalents are the names still in use. The fourth circle is left unfilled in the text as it stands here, which is the place the sun holds in the ancient order.

The book builds man out of seven materials: flesh from earth, blood from dew, eyes from the sun, bones from stone, intelligence from the angels and cloud, veins and hair from grass, and soul from God's breath and the wind. Genesis 2:7 gives two, the dust of the ground and the breath of life. The seven-part scheme belongs to this book.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ἀνατολή, δύσις, ἄρκτος, μεσημβρία (anatole, dysis, arktos, mesembria)
translationNotes.note: The text says the name was taken from the four quarters. In Greek those four are anatole for east, dysis for west, arktos for north and mesembria for south, and their opening letters are alpha, delta, alpha and mu, which spell Adam. The Hebrew name works another way: adam is man, from adamah, the ground, at Genesis 2:7.

The book ranks Adam as a second angel placed on earth, honourable and great and appointed to rule. Psalm 8:5 says man was made a little lower than the angels and crowned with glory and honour, and Genesis 1:28 hands him dominion. The title second angel is this book's own.

Genesis 3:20 says Adam called his wife's name Eve because she was the mother of all living, and the Hebrew name is built on the word for living. This chapter gives the same explanation in shorter form, saying he called her mother.

Setting two roads before a man is the standard shape of instruction here and in Scripture. Deuteronomy 30:15-19 sets life and good against death and evil and orders a choice, and Psalm 1:6 divides the way of the righteous from the way of the ungodly.

stories.keyTakeaway: God runs through the days of creation: trees and Paradise, then the lights set on their circles under their Greek names, then sea creatures and birds and beasts, then man, built of seven components, named Adam from the four quarters and given a wife from his rib.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 31
summaryBullets: Adam has life on earth, and I created a garden in Eden in the east, that he should observe the testament and keep the command. (31:1).
I made the heavens open to him, that he should see the angels singing the song of victory, and the gloomless light. (31:2).
And he was continuously in paradise, and the devil understood that I wanted to create another world, because Adam was lord on earth, to rule and control it. (31:3).

The devil is the evil spirit of the lower places, as a fugitive he made Sotona from the heavens as his name was Satanail (Satan), thus he became different from the angels, (but his nature) did not change (his) intelligence as far as (his) understanding of righteous and sinful (things). (31:4).
And he understood his condemnation and the sin which he had sinned before, therefore he conceived thought against Adam, in such form he entered and seduced Eva (Eve), but did not touch Adam. (31:5).
But I cursed ignorance, but what I had blessed previously, those I did not curse, I cursed not man, nor the earth, nor other creatures, but man's evil fruit, and his works. (31:6).
crossRefs: Genesis 2:15-17: God puts the man in the garden to dress it and keep it and gives him one command, not to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
Genesis 3:1-6: The serpent speaks to the woman, she takes of the fruit and eats, and she gives to her husband with her and he eats.
Genesis 3:17-19: The ground is cursed for man's sake, thorns and thistles are named, and he eats bread in the sweat of his face until he returns to the ground.
2 Corinthians 11:3: Paul writes of the serpent beguiling Eve through his subtilty, and fears the same corrupting of the mind.
1 Timothy 2:14: Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression, the same distinction this chapter draws.

translationNotes.note: The book says he was called Satanail in heaven and Sotona once he was thrown out, so the change of name marks a change of standing. The syllable that drops away is the il that stands for el, the ending on the names of angels.

Berit means a covenant, a binding agreement with terms attached, which older English renders testament. Genesis 2:16-17 gives Adam a single term to keep with a stated penalty, and this chapter calls that arrangement a covenant.

Genesis 3:6 has the woman give to her husband with her and he ate. 1 Timothy 2:14 says Adam was not deceived while the woman was. This book says the approach was made to her alone and that Adam was never spoken to.

The line sorts out what was cursed and what was not. Genesis 3:14 curses the serpent and Genesis 3:17 curses the ground for man's sake. This book says God cursed neither the man nor the earth nor any creature, only man's evil fruit and his works, and puts ignorance at the head of the list.

translationNotes.term: The evil spirit of the lower places
translationNotes.note: The book puts the devil below rather than in the heavens, in the region it earlier called the lower foundation. Ephesians 2:2 places him in the air and Ephesians 6:12 sets the struggle against spiritual wickedness in high places, so Scripture does not pin him to one level.

translationNotes.term: Because I wanted to create another world
translationNotes.note: The motive given is jealousy over an order in which Adam was lord on earth. Wisdom 2:24 states the same motive in one line, that through envy of the devil came death into the world.

stories.keyTakeaway: Adam is set in the garden in the east under a command to keep, with heaven left open above him. The devil, thrown out and renamed, works out his own condemnation, turns on Adam, and enters to seduce Eve while leaving Adam untouched.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 32
summaryBullets: I said to him: Earth you are, and into the earth from where I took you you shalt go, and I will not ruin you, but send you from where I took you. (32:1).
Then I can again receive you at My second presence. (32:2).
And I blessed all my creatures visible (physical) and invisible (spiritual). And Adam was five and half hours in paradise. (32:3).
And I blessed the seventh day, which is the Sabbath, on which he rested from all his works. (32:4).
crossRefs: Genesis 3:19: Dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return, the sentence this chapter is repeating.
Genesis 2:1-3: God ends his work on the seventh day and rests, and blesses and sanctifies the day because in it he rested from all his work.
Exodus 20:8-11: Remember the sabbath day to keep it holy, for in six days the LORD made heaven and earth and rested the seventh day.
Ecclesiastes 12:7: The dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
Acts 1:11: This same Jesus shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven, the return this chapter calls a second presence.

translationNotes.note: Parousia means a presence or an arrival, and it was the ordinary word for a king or governor coming in state to a city. The New Testament uses it of the return of Christ at Matthew 24:27 and 1 Thessalonians 4:15, and this book uses the same idea of a second coming.

translationNotes.term: Five and half hours in paradise
translationNotes.note: The figure belongs to this book. Genesis gives no length of time for Adam's stay in the garden between his making and his expulsion. The number is stated flatly and nothing in the narrative supports or explains it.

The sentence at Genesis 3:19 turns on a pun the English cannot carry. Adam, the man, goes back into adamah, the ground. The name and the sentence are built from the same letters, which is why the line closes a circle rather than simply announcing a death.

translationNotes.term: The seventh day, which is the Sabbath
translationNotes.note: Shabbat comes from a verb meaning to stop or cease. Genesis 2:2-3 has God cease and then bless and set the day apart, and Exodus 20:11 makes that the reason attached to the fourth commandment. This chapter states it in a single line.

Genesis 3:19 sends the man back to the dust and stops there. This book adds an explicit promise not to destroy him and a stated intention to receive him again later, which the Genesis sentence does not carry at that point.

stories.keyTakeaway: God tells Adam he goes back to the earth he was taken from and will be received again at a second coming. The chapter says Adam spent five and a half hours in paradise, and it closes by blessing the seventh day as the Sabbath.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 33
summaryBullets: And I appointed the eighth day also, that the eighth day should be the first-created after my work, and that (the first seven) revolve in the form of the seventh thousand, and that at the beginning of the eighth thousand there should be a time of not-counting, endless, with neither years nor months nor weeks nor days nor hours. (33:1).

And now, Enoch, all that I have told you, all that you have understood, all that you have seen of heavenly things, all that you have seen on earth, and all that I have written in books by my great wisdom, all these things I have devised and created from the uppermost foundation to the lower and to the end, and there is no counsellor nor inheritor to my creations. (33:2).
I am self-eternal, not made with hands, and without change. (33:3).
My thought is my counsellor, my wisdom and my word are made, and my eyes observe all things how they stand here and tremble with terror. (33:4).
If I turn away my face, then all things will be destroyed. (33:5).
And apply your mind, Enoch, and know him who is speaking to you, and take from there the books which you yourself have written. (33:6).

And I give you Samuil and Raguil, who led you up, and the books, and go down to earth, and tell your sons all that I have told you, and all that you have seen, from the lower heaven up to my throne, and all the troops. (33:7).
For I created all forces, and there is none that resists me or that does not subject himself to me. For all subject themselves to my monarchy, and labour for my sole rule. (33:8).
Give them the books of the handwriting, and they will read (them) and will know me for the creator of all things, and will understand how there is no other God but me. (33:9).
And let them distribute the books of your handwriting–children to children, generation to generation, nations to nations. (33:10).
And I will give you, Enoch, my intercessor, the archistratege Michael, for the handwritings of your fathers Adam, Seth, Enos, Cainan, Mahaleleel, and Jared your father. (33:11).
crossRefs: Psalm 90:4: A thousand years in thy sight are but as yesterday when it is past, and as a watch in the night.
2 Peter 3:8: One day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.
Romans 11:34: Who has known the mind of the Lord, or who has been his counsellor, the question this chapter answers with a flat none.
Genesis 5:1-20: The line from Adam through Seth, Enos, Cainan, Mahalaleel and Jared down to Enoch, the fathers named at the close of this chapter.
Hebrews 4:9-10: There remains a rest for the people of God, and the one who has entered that rest has ceased from his own works as God did from his.

translationNotes.note: The book runs the seven days of creation as seven thousand years and then adds an eighth in which nothing is counted, no years, months, weeks, days or hours. Psalm 90:4 and 2 Peter 3:8 both set a thousand years beside a single day, which is the equivalence this scheme is built on.

The two guides who carried Enoch up are finally named here at the end of the journey, having been called only the two men until now. Raguil stands close to the Raguel listed among the holy angels at 1 Enoch 20:4.

Made without hands is a deliberate contrast with an idol, which is handmade by definition. Mark 14:58 and Hebrews 9:11 both use the term of a sanctuary not made with hands, and Acts 17:24 says God does not dwell in temples made with hands.

translationNotes.term: If I turn away my face
translationNotes.note: Psalm 104:29 says the same of every living thing: thou hidest thy face, they are troubled, thou takest away their breath, they die. Holding the world in being is described as an act that continues rather than one that was finished at the start.

translationNotes.term: Children to children, generation to generation
translationNotes.note: Copying a text inside a family is how books survived. Deuteronomy 6:6-9 orders the words taught to children, spoken at home and on the road, and bound as a sign, which is the same distribution plan in different words.

translationNotes.term: Adam, Seth, Enos, Cainan, Mahaleleel, and Jared
translationNotes.note: The six generations before Enoch, in the order Genesis 5:1-18 gives them. This book credits every one of them with writings that Michael is to keep, which Scripture does not report of any of them.

stories.keyTakeaway: God sets an eighth day beyond the seven and an eighth thousand years in which time stops being counted. He declares himself without counsellor or heir, sends Enoch back with the books, and names the fathers whose writings Michael is to keep.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 34
summaryBullets: They have rejected my commandments and my yoke, worthless seed has come up, not fearing God, and they would not bow down to me, but have begun to bow down to vain gods, and denied my unity, and have laden the whole earth with untruths, offences, abominable lecheries, namely one with another, and all manner of other unclean wickedness, which are disgusting to relate. (34:1).
And therefore I will bring down a deluge upon the earth and will destroy all men, and the whole earth will crumble together into great darkness. (34:2).
crossRefs: Genesis 6:5-7: God sees that the wickedness of man is great and every imagination of his heart only evil continually, and says he will destroy man from the earth.
Genesis 6:11-13: The earth is corrupt before God and filled with violence, and God tells Noah the end of all flesh has come before him.
Deuteronomy 6:4: Hear, O Israel, the LORD our God is one LORD, the confession of God's oneness this chapter says the generations denied.
Romans 1:24-27: Men exchange the truth of God for a lie, worship the creature rather than the Creator, and are given up to acts against nature.
Jubilees 5:1-4: The parallel account has the earth corrupted, lawlessness increasing, and God resolving to destroy man and all flesh together.

translationNotes.note: A yoke is the wooden beam harnessing a working animal, and it is the standard image for living under someone's rule. Jeremiah 2:20 has Israel break its yoke and burst its bonds, and Matthew 11:29-30 turns the same image around into a yoke that is easy.

translationNotes.term: Abominable lecheries, namely one with another
translationNotes.note: This is the 1896 English translation's wording for sexual acts between men. Leviticus 18:22 and Leviticus 20:13 name the act and set its penalty, and Romans 1:27 describes men leaving the natural use of the woman and burning in their lust one toward another. The chapter lists it among the grounds for the flood.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ יְהוָה אֶחָד (YHWH Eloheinu YHWH echad)
translationNotes.note: The confession that the LORD is one comes from Deuteronomy 6:4 and is called the Shema after its opening word, Hear. Denying his unity here means going after other gods, not making a philosophical mistake, which is why it sits in a list with idols and lawlessness.
Mabbul is used in Scripture only of the flood in Noah's day, at Genesis 6:17 and Psalm 29:10. The Greek Septuagint renders it kataklysmos, which is where the English word cataclysm comes from.

Seed means offspring, a whole line of descent rather than particular men. Genesis 6:5 describes the same generations as men whose every imagination was only evil continually, and this book compresses that verdict into two words.

stories.keyTakeaway: God tells Enoch what the coming generations do: reject his commands, bow to vain gods, deny that he is one, and fill the earth with sexual wickedness. For that he says he will bring a flood down and destroy all men.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 35
summaryBullets: Behold from their seed shall arise another generation, much afterwards, but of them many will be very insatiate. (35:1).

He who raises that generation, (shall) reveal to them the books of your handwriting, of your fathers, (to them) to whom he must point out the guardianship of the world, to the faithful men and workers of my pleasure, who do not acknowledge my name in vain. (35:2).
And they shall tell another generation, and those (others) having read shall be glorified thereafter, more than the first. (35:3).
crossRefs: Exodus 20:7: Thou shalt not take the name of the LORD thy God in vain, the command this chapter's closing phrase comes from.
Genesis 9:1: God blesses Noah and his sons and tells them to be fruitful and multiply and replenish the earth, the generation raised after the flood.
Daniel 12:4: Shut up the words and seal the book to the time of the end, so a text is deliberately held back for a later generation.
Psalm 78:5-6: A testimony was appointed in Jacob so that the generation to come might know it and the children not yet born declare it to theirs.
1 Enoch 93:9-10: An apostate generation arises, and at its close the elect are chosen to receive sevenfold instruction concerning all creation.

translationNotes.note: An old English word meaning unable to be satisfied. The charge is appetite without limit rather than any single act, and it is what separates the many from the faithful few inside the same generation.

The faithful men are handed charge of the world along with the books, so keeping the text and keeping the creation are set out as one commission. Genesis 2:15 puts the man in the garden to dress it and to keep it, using two verbs for the same pairing.

translationNotes.term: Who do not acknowledge my name in vain
translationNotes.note: The Hebrew word in Exodus 20:7 means emptiness, falsehood or worthlessness. Taking the name in vain covers swearing falsely by it and using it as an empty formula, not only cursing with it.

The phrase runs through the whole second half of the book. What is handed down is Enoch's own hand, the physical copy he wrote out in the heavens, which is why the text keeps stressing copying and distribution rather than memory.

translationNotes.term: Glorified thereafter, more than the first
translationNotes.note: The later readers are ranked above the earlier ones. Haggai 2:9 makes the same comparison about a building, saying the glory of the latter house shall be greater than of the former.

stories.keyTakeaway: God says another generation will rise later from the same seed, many of them greedy, and that the books will be shown to the faithful among them, the men given charge of the world who do not take his name in vain.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 36
summaryBullets: Now, Enoch, I give you the term of thirty days to spend in your house, and tell your sons and all your household, that all may hear from my face what is told them by you, that they may read and understand, how there is no other God but me. (36:1).
And that they may always keep my commandments, and begin to read and take in the books of your handwriting. (36:2).
And after thirty days I shall send my angel for you, and he will take you from earth and from your sons to me. (36:3).
crossRefs: Deuteronomy 31:24-26: Moses finishes writing the words in a book and orders it placed beside the ark as a witness, the same act of committing a text before departure.
Deuteronomy 32:45-47: Moses tells the people to set their hearts on all the words and to command their children to keep them, because it is their life.
Joshua 23:14: Joshua tells the people he is going the way of all the earth, and charges them while he still can.
Deuteronomy 4:35: Unto thee it was shewed, that thou mightest know that the LORD he is God, and there is none else beside him.
Acts 20:25-32: Paul tells the elders they will see his face no more and commits them to God and to the word before he goes.

translationNotes.note: A fixed period is set aside for handing the teaching over. Thirty days is also the mourning period for Moses at Deuteronomy 34:8 and for Aaron at Numbers 20:29, so it is a standard span in this reckoning rather than a round guess.

Enoch's sons are to hear from God's face through him, which makes him a carrier of words that are not his. That is the standard claim of a prophet, stated at Deuteronomy 18:18 as words put into a man's mouth.

translationNotes.term: There is no other God but me
translationNotes.note: The sentence recurs through this book and every stretch of instruction comes back to it. Deuteronomy 4:35 and Isaiah 45:5 both put it in the same flat form, that there is none else.

translationNotes.term: I shall send my angel for you
translationNotes.note: The removal is scheduled in advance. Genesis 5:24 says only that God took him, with no notice and no date. This book gives thirty days' warning and names an angel as the one sent to fetch him.
The order is to read them and absorb them. Nehemiah 8:8 describes what that looked like in practice, reading distinctly and giving the sense so that the people understood the reading.

stories.keyTakeaway: God gives Enoch a term of thirty days at home to tell his sons and his household everything and to put the books in their hands, and then says he will send an angel to take him off the earth for good.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 37
summaryBullets: And the Lord called upon one of the older angels, terrible and menacing, and placed him by me, in appearance white as snow, and his hands like ice, having the appearance of great frost, and he froze my face, because I could not endure the terror of the Lord, just as it is not possible to endure A stove's fire and the sun's heat, and the frost of the air. (37:1).
And the Lord said to me: Enoch, if your face be not frozen here, no man will be able to behold your face. (37:2).
crossRefs: Exodus 34:29-35: Moses comes down from Sinai not knowing his face shone, the people are afraid to come near him, and he puts a veil over it.
2 Corinthians 3:7-13: The ministration written on stones came with such glory that Israel could not look steadily at Moses' face, so he covered it.
Exodus 33:20: Thou canst not see my face, for there shall no man see me and live.
Matthew 17:2: He was transfigured before them, his face shining as the sun and his raiment white as the light.
Daniel 10:8-9: The prophet is left with no strength and his comeliness turned to corruption, and he falls on his face in a deep sleep.

translationNotes.note: The freezing is presented as a practical measure and not a punishment. Enoch's face has to be damped down so that people can bear to look at him. Exodus 34:30 reports the same problem after Sinai and solves it with a veil instead.

The comparison is to a domestic oven, a clay dome heated from the inside with dung or brushwood until the walls glow, then used to bake bread against the hot surface. Standing beside one was the fiercest heat in ordinary daily life.

The book ranks angels by seniority as well as by office. Scripture distinguishes cherubim, seraphim and archangels but never describes older and younger among them, and the ranking here belongs to this book.

Pachad is dread, the physical reaction rather than reverence. Isaiah 2:10 tells men to hide in the rock for fear of the LORD and the glory of his majesty, and 2 Corinthians 5:11 uses the phrase the terror of the Lord outright.

translationNotes.term: White as snow, hands like ice
translationNotes.note: The angel is described entirely in terms of cold, which is unusual. Scripture's angels arrive with fire and lightning, as at Daniel 10:6 and Psalm 104:4. This one is built for the single job of cooling a man down.

stories.keyTakeaway: An angel white as snow with hands like ice is set beside Enoch and freezes his face before he is sent down, because a man who has looked at the Lord's face could not otherwise be looked at by anyone on earth.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 38
summaryBullets: And the Lord said to those men who first led me up: Let Enoch go down on to earth with you, and await him till the determined day. (38:1).
And they placed me by night on my bed. (38:2).

And Mathusal (Methuselah) expecting my coming, keeping watch by day and by night at my bed, was filled with awe when he heard my coming, and I told him, Let all my household come together, that I tell them everything. (38:3).
crossRefs: Genesis 5:22: Enoch walked with God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters.
Genesis 49:1-2: Jacob calls his sons together to tell them what shall befall them in the last days, the same summoning before a father goes.
Deuteronomy 31:28: Moses tells the elders and officers to gather to him so that he can speak these words in their ears and call heaven and earth to record.
Joshua 24:1-2: Joshua gathers all the tribes to Shechem and calls for the elders, heads, judges and officers, and they present themselves before God.
1 Enoch 81:5-6: Seven holy ones set Enoch down at the door of his house and tell him to teach his children, leaving him with them for one year.

translationNotes.note: The return runs to a schedule fixed thirty days earlier. The book keeps dates all the way through and ends by giving the month and the day of Enoch's final removal, so this is a calendar entry and not a vague promise.

translationNotes.term: Keeping watch by day and by night at my bed
translationNotes.note: Methuselah has been sitting beside an empty bed since his father vanished. The book opened with Enoch ordering that nobody search for him, and this line shows what obeying that order looked like from inside the house.
The book began with Enoch asleep on this same bed when the two men appeared at his head, and it puts him back on it. The whole journey is framed between one night and another in the same room.

The group summoned is not only his sons. It takes in wives, servants, dependants and everyone living under his roof, which is why the later chapters have him addressing elders and a whole people as well as children.

translationNotes.term: Await him till the determined day
translationNotes.note: The two guides are told to wait rather than to leave, so they stay on earth for the thirty days. The book says later that they are standing there waiting when the time runs out, which is how it keeps the schedule in view.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch is sent back down and set on his own bed at night. Methuselah has kept watch beside that bed day and night and is struck with awe when he hears his father come, and Enoch calls the whole household together.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 39
summaryBullets: Oh my children, my beloved ones, hear the admonition of your father, as much as is according to the Lord's will. (39:1).
I have been let come to you to-day, and announce to you, not from my lips, but from the Lord's lips, all that is and was and all that is now, and all that will be till judgment-day. (39:2).

For the Lord has let me come to you, you hear therefore the words of my lips, of a man made big for you, but I am one who has seen the Lord's face, like iron made to glow from fire it sends forth sparks and burns. (39:3).
You look now upon my eyes, (the eyes) of a man big with meaning for you, but I have seen the Lord's eyes, shining like the sun's rays and filling the eyes of man with awe. (39:4).
You see now, my children, the right hand of a man that helps you, but I have seen the Lord's right hand filling heaven as he helped me. (39:5).
You see the compass of my work like your own, but I have seen the Lord's limitless and perfect compass, which has no end. (39:6).
You hear the words of my lips, as I heard the words of the Lord, like great thunder incessantly with hurling of clouds. (39:7).

And now, my children, hear the discourses of the father of the earth, how fearful and awful it is to come before the face of the ruler of the earth, how much more terrible and awful it is to come before the face of the ruler of heaven, the controller (judge) of quick and dead, and of the heavenly troops. Who can endure that endless pain? (39:8).
crossRefs: Jeremiah 1:9: The LORD puts forth his hand, touches the prophet's mouth, and says, Behold, I have put my words in thy mouth.
Deuteronomy 18:18: I will raise them up a Prophet and will put my words in his mouth, and he shall speak all that I command him.
Revelation 1:14-16: His eyes are as a flame of fire, his feet like fine brass, his voice as the sound of many waters and his countenance as the sun.
Exodus 33:20-23: No man can see God's face and live, so Moses is put in a cleft of the rock and shown only what passes by.
Acts 10:42: He commanded us to preach and to testify that it is he which was ordained of God to be the Judge of quick and dead.

translationNotes.term: The controller of quick and dead
translationNotes.note: Quick is old English for living. Acts 10:42 and 2 Timothy 4:1 both use the phrase of the one who judges the living and the dead, so the title Enoch uses here is the standard one and not a coinage.

Compass here means extent or reach, the ground a thing covers, not the drawing instrument. Proverbs 8:27 uses the same English word the other way, of a circle set on the face of the deep, and both senses survive.

Enoch calls himself the father of the earth, meaning the elder of the line, since the book has him addressing every household then living through his own sons. Scripture gives the title father to the founder of a people, as at Genesis 17:5.

translationNotes.term: Not from my lips, but from the Lord's lips
translationNotes.note: The distinction is the standard prophetic one. Jeremiah 1:9 has God put the words in the man's mouth, and Deuteronomy 18:18 makes that the mark of a true prophet, that he says what he was given and nothing else.

One Hebrew word covers voice, sound and thunder, so Scripture can call thunder the voice of God without reaching for a figure of speech. Psalm 29:3-9 runs an entire storm as the voice of the LORD, seven times over.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch tells his children that what they are about to hear comes from the Lord's lips and not his own, and he sets his own face, eyes, hand and reach beside God's one at a time to show how much greater the audience above is.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 40
summaryBullets: And now, my children, I know all things, for this (is) from the Lord's lips, and this my eyes have seen, from beginning to end. (40:1).
I know all things, and have written all things into books, the heavens and their end, and their plenitude, and all the armies and their marchings. (40:2).
I have measured and described the stars, the great countless multitude (of them). (40:3).
What man has seen their revolutions, and their entrances? For not even the angels see their number, while I have written all their names. (40:4).

And I measured the sun's circle, and measured its rays, counted the hours, I wrote down too all things that go over the earth, I have written the things that are nourished, and all seed sown and unsown, which the earth produces and all plants, and every grass and every flower, and their sweet smells, and their names, and the dwelling-places of the clouds, and their composition, and their wings, and how they bear rain and raindrops. (40:5).

And I investigated all things, and wrote the road of the thunder and of the lightning, and they showed me the keys and their guardians, their rise, the way they go; it is let out (gently) in measure by a chain, lest by A heavy chain and violence it hurl down the angry clouds and destroy all things on earth. (40:6).

I wrote the treasure-houses of the snow, and the store-houses of the cold and the frosty airs, and I observed their season's key-holder, he fills the clouds with them, and does not exhaust the treasure-houses. (40:7).

And I wrote the resting-places of the winds and observed and saw how their key-holders bear weighing-scales and measures; first, they put them in (one) weighing-scale, then in the other the weights and let them out according to measure cunningly over the whole earth, lest by heavy breathing they make the earth to rock. (40:8).

And I measured out the whole earth, its mountains, and all hills, fields, trees, stones, rivers, all existing things I wrote down, the height from earth to the seventh heaven, and downwards to the very lowest hell, and the judgment-place, and the very great, open and weeping hell. (40:9).
And I saw how the prisoners are in pain, expecting the limitless judgment. (40:10).
And I wrote down all those being judged by the judge, and all their judgment (and sentences) and all their works. (40:11).
crossRefs: Job 28:25-26: God makes a weight for the wind, weighs the waters by measure, makes a decree for the rain and a way for the lightning of the thunder.
Isaiah 40:12: Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, meted out heaven with the span, and weighed the mountains in scales.
Job 38:34-38: God asks whether Job can lift his voice to the clouds, send lightnings that report back to him, or number the clouds in wisdom.
1 Enoch 41:3-6: Enoch is shown the secret chambers of the winds, the thunder and the lightning, and how they are divided to blow over the earth.
Revelation 20:12-13: The books are opened, the dead are judged out of the things written in them, and every man is judged according to his works.

translationNotes.term: Let out in measure by a chain
translationNotes.note: The lightning is described as a weight lowered on a chain, released gently so that it does not crash down and wreck what it lands on. The picture is a hoist or a well bucket, ordinary machinery, applied to the weather.

A balance is two pans hung from a beam. Job 28:25 says God made a weight for the wind and weighed the waters by measure, and Isaiah 40:12 weighs the mountains in scales, so issuing weather by weight is not new with this book.

Every store in this book has a keeper holding the key: the winds, the cold, the snow, the seasons, the gates of hell. Revelation 1:18 and Revelation 9:1 both put keys into a named figure's hand, so the office exists in Scripture even though the departments here are the book's own.

English hell renders more than one word. Sheol in Hebrew and hades in Greek mean the place of the dead in general. Gehenna, the word Jesus uses, is the Greek form of the Valley of Hinnom outside Jerusalem, where 2 Kings 23:10 says men made their sons and daughters pass through the fire to Molech and where Jeremiah 7:31 places the high places of Tophet.

translationNotes.term: Not even the angels see their number
translationNotes.note: Enoch is credited with knowledge the angels do not have, which follows the claim made at the throne that God told him what he had told no angel. Ranking a man above the heavenly host is stated more than once in this book.

translationNotes.term: The height from earth to the seventh heaven
translationNotes.note: The measurement is claimed and the figure is never given. This book hands out numbers freely everywhere else, so the silence stands out. What Enoch reports is that he measured it and wrote it down, not what it came to.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch reports what he wrote down: the name of every star, the sun's circuit, every growing thing, the roads of thunder and lightning let out on a chain, the winds weighed on scales, and the distance from earth to the seventh heaven and down to the lowest hell.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 41
summaryBullets: And I saw all forefathers from (all) time with Adam and Eva (Eve), and I sighed and broke into tears and said of the ruin of their dishonour: (41:1).
Woe is me for my infirmity and (for that) of my forefathers, and thought in my heart and said: (41:2).
Blessed (is) the man who has not been born or who has been born and shall not sin before the Lord's face, that he come not into this place, nor bring the yoke of this place. (41:3).
crossRefs: Ecclesiastes 4:2-3: Better than the living and the dead is the one who has not yet been, who has not seen the evil work done under the sun.
Job 3:11-16: Job asks why he did not die at birth, and says he would then have been at rest with the kings and counsellors of the earth.
Jeremiah 20:14-18: The prophet curses the day he was born and asks why he came out of the womb to see labour and sorrow.
Matthew 26:24: It had been good for that man if he had not been born, the same measure applied to one man by name.
2 Esdras 4:12: It were better that we were not at all, than that we should live still in wickedness and suffer without knowing why.

translationNotes.note: A yoke is a burden fastened on that cannot be shrugged off. The chapter uses it of the condition of the condemned rather than of any punishment handed out, so what is pictured is a load carried permanently rather than a sentence served.

translationNotes.term: All forefathers from all time with Adam and Eva
translationNotes.note: The book puts the first parents among the condemned and has Enoch weep over them. Genesis reports their expulsion and their deaths and says nothing about where they went afterward. This scene is supplied here.

translationNotes.term: Blessed is the man who has not been born
translationNotes.note: The saying has a known shape. Ecclesiastes 4:2-3 ranks the unborn above both the living and the dead, and Job 3:11-16 has a man wish he had died at birth. Matthew 26:24 applies the same measure to a single named man.

Infirmity here means weakness of the whole nature rather than an illness. Enoch puts himself in with the forefathers he is weeping over, which is why the sentence begins with woe is me before it reaches them at all.
A formal cry that opens a lament, not a mood. Isaiah 6:5 uses it when the prophet sees the Lord and says he is undone, and Jeremiah 4:31 and Micah 7:1 use it to begin set speeches of grief.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch says he saw the forefathers with Adam and Eve among them in the place of the condemned, and that he wept. He calls blessed the man never born, or born and never sinning, who never has to come there at all.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 42
summaryBullets: I saw the key-holders and guards of the gates of hell standing, like great serpents, and their faces like extinguishing lamps, and their eyes of fire, their sharp teeth, and I saw all the Lord's works, how they are right, while the works of man are some (good), and others bad, and in their works are known those who lie evilly. (42:1).
crossRefs: Revelation 1:18: I have the keys of hell and of death, so the keys are held by one named holder and not left loose.
Revelation 9:1-2: A star fallen from heaven is given the key of the bottomless pit, and smoke as of a great furnace comes up when it is opened.
Matthew 7:16-20: Ye shall know them by their fruits, for a corrupt tree cannot bring forth good fruit and a good tree cannot bring forth evil.
Deuteronomy 32:4: He is the Rock, his work is perfect, for all his ways are judgment, a God of truth and without iniquity.
Isaiah 27:1: The LORD punishes leviathan the piercing serpent, that crooked serpent, and slays the dragon that is in the sea.

translationNotes.note: A city gate was where its power sat: courts met there and armies were stopped there. Isaiah 38:10 speaks of the gates of the grave and Matthew 16:18 of the gates of hell, so the phrase names a stronghold and its authority rather than a doorway.

A lamp going out was a shallow clay dish of olive oil with a wick in the lip, guttering and smoking as the oil ran down. The image is failing light and smoke rather than plain darkness, which is why the eyes of fire are set against it.

Guards described as serpents. Scripture uses serpent imagery for the adversary at Genesis 3:1 and Revelation 12:9 and for the sea monster at Isaiah 27:1. Making the gatekeepers themselves serpents is this book's own picture.

Yashar means straight, level, upright, the opposite of crooked. Deuteronomy 32:4 says all God's ways are judgment and there is no iniquity in him, and the contrast this chapter draws is between work that is straight and work that is half one thing and half the other.

translationNotes.term: In their works are known those who lie evilly
translationNotes.note: The test is conduct, not speech. Matthew 7:16-20 puts it as knowing a tree by its fruit, and this chapter says a man's record is what gives him away even when his words do not.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch sees the gatekeepers of hell, serpent-like, with faces like guttering lamps, eyes of fire and sharp teeth. He says every work of God is straight while men's works are mixed, and that a man's works are what expose his lying.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 43
summaryBullets: I, my children, measured and wrote out every work and every measure and every righteous judgment. (43:1).

As (one) year is more honourable than another, so is (one) man more honourable than another, some for great possessions, some for wisdom of heart, some for particular intellect, some for cunning, one for silence of lip, another for cleanliness, one for strength, another for comeliness, one for youth, another for sharp wit, one for shape of body, another for sensibility, let it be heard everywhere, but there is none better than he who fears God, he shall be more glorious in time to come. (43:2).
crossRefs: Proverbs 1:7: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and instruction.
Ecclesiastes 12:13: Fear God and keep his commandments, for this is the whole duty of man, given as the conclusion of the whole matter.
Jeremiah 9:23-24: Let not the wise glory in his wisdom, nor the mighty in his might, nor the rich in his riches, but in knowing the LORD.
Proverbs 31:30: Favour is deceitful and beauty is vain, but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised.
Sirach 10:19-24: Honour is weighed by whether a man fears the Lord, and a poor man with understanding is ranked above a rich man without it.

translationNotes.term: As one year is more honourable than another
translationNotes.note: Years were ranked by what happened in them, a harvest year against a famine year, a jubilee against an ordinary one. Leviticus 25:10-12 sets the fiftieth year apart from every other, so the comparison had a concrete sense for the first hearers.

In older English cunning means skill or knowing how, with none of the modern suggestion of trickery. Exodus 31:4 uses it of a craftsman devising cunning works in gold, silver and brass, so on this list it names competence.
Being able to keep quiet is listed as a distinction on the same footing as strength and wealth. Proverbs 17:28 makes the same point, that even a fool is counted wise while he holds his peace.
The fear of the LORD is not fright but a settled reckoning of who God is, which Proverbs 1:7 calls the beginning of knowledge. Ecclesiastes 12:13 ends its whole argument on the same two words.

In older English sensibility means the capacity to feel and perceive, closer to sensitivity than to good sense. It closes a list that runs from possessions down to the shape of a man's body, and every item on it is a natural advantage rather than a moral one.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch lists the things that make one man count for more than another, from property and wisdom through strength, looks and quick wit, and then says none of them beats fearing God, which is what will tell in the time to come.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 44
summaryBullets: The Lord with his hands having created man, in the likeness of his own face, the Lord made him small and great. (44:1).

Whoever reviles the ruler's face, and abhors the Lord's face, has despised the Lord's face, and he who vents anger on any man without injury, the Lord's great anger will cut him down, he who spits on the face of man reproachfully, will be cut down at the Lord's great judgment. (44:2).

Blessed is the man who does not direct his heart with malice against any man, and helps the injured and condemned, and raises the broken down, and shall do charity to the needy, because on the day of the great judgment every weight, every measure and every makeweight (will be) as in the market, that is to say (they are) hung on scales and stand in the market, (and every one) shall learn his own measure, and according to his measure shall take his reward. (44:3).
crossRefs: Genesis 1:26-27: God makes man in his own image, in the image of God created he him, male and female created he them.
Genesis 9:6: Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed, for in the image of God made he man.
James 3:9-10: With the same tongue we bless God and curse men who are made after the similitude of God, and out of one mouth come blessing and cursing.
Matthew 5:22: Whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment, and whoever says Thou fool in danger of hell fire.
Leviticus 19:35-36: Do no unrighteousness in judgment, in meteyard, in weight or in measure, but keep just balances, just weights, a just ephah and a just hin.

translationNotes.term: Spits on the face of man
translationNotes.note: Spitting in the face was the strongest public insult available. Numbers 12:14 uses it as the measure of disgrace, asking whether a woman whose father had spit in her face should not be ashamed seven days, and Deuteronomy 25:9 makes it part of a legal ceremony against a man who refuses his duty.

translationNotes.term: Every weight, every measure and every makeweight
translationNotes.note: The Hebrew word for a weight is stone, because weights were cut stones carried in a bag. Deuteronomy 25:13-15 forbids keeping a stone and a stone, a heavy one for buying and a light one for selling, and Proverbs 11:1 calls a false balance an abomination.

Trade was done in the open, at the gate or in the market square, and the scales stood where a buyer could watch the weighing. The judgment is described as that same public weighing, with every man seeing his own measure go on the beam.

The face stands for the person and his standing, so reviling a ruler's face means insulting the office in public. Exodus 22:28 forbids reviling a ruler of the people, and this chapter runs the line from a man's face to the likeness of God in him.

Both at once. The creation account earlier in this book already called man small in greatness and great in smallness, so this line is picking up a phrase the book set down before rather than assigning a rank.

A makeweight is the small extra piece dropped into a pan to bring a load up to the mark. Naming it beside the weight and the measure closes off the last way a trader could cheat, which is why the list runs to three items and not two.

stories.keyTakeaway: Because man was made in God's likeness, insulting a man's face insults God's. Enoch warns against anger without injury and against spitting in a man's face, and says the last judgment will weigh every man on public scales.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 45
summaryBullets: Whoever hastens to make offerings before the Lord's face, the Lord for his part will hasten that offering by granting of his work. (45:1).
But whoever increases his lamp before the Lord's face and make not true judgment, the Lord will (not) increase his treasure in the realm of the highest. (45:2).

When the Lord demands bread, or candles, or (the )flesh (of beasts), or any other sacrifice, then that is nothing; but God demands pure hearts, and with all that (only) tests the heart of man. (45:3).
crossRefs: 1 Samuel 15:22: Hath the LORD as great delight in burnt offerings as in obeying the voice of the LORD? To obey is better than sacrifice.
Psalm 51:16-17: Thou desirest not sacrifice, else would I give it, for the sacrifices of God are a broken spirit and a contrite heart.
Hosea 6:6: I desired mercy and not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.
Isaiah 1:11-17: God asks what the multitude of sacrifices is to him, and tells them instead to cease from evil, learn to do well and judge the fatherless.
Micah 6:6-8: The question of what to bring is answered plainly: to do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God.

translationNotes.note: Lamps were given to a sanctuary and kept burning as an offering in themselves. Exodus 27:20-21 requires pure beaten olive oil so the lamp burns from evening to morning continually and Leviticus 24:2-4 repeats the order, so increasing a lamp means enlarging that gift.
Not wax candles. The word covers the clay oil lamp, a shallow dish with a pinched lip holding a wick in olive oil, which is what every house and every sanctuary burned for light.

The line does not abolish offerings. This same book ends with Enoch's sons building an altar and sacrificing oxen. What it says is that the offering counts for nothing without the heart, which is the point 1 Samuel 15:22 and Hosea 6:6 both make.

Bachan is the word for assaying metal, putting it in the fire to find out what it actually is. Psalm 26:2 asks God to examine and prove and try the reins and the heart, and Jeremiah 17:10 says the LORD searches the heart and tries the reins.

The answer is described as matching the speed of the gift, quickly given and quickly returned. Proverbs 3:9-10 makes the same link between honouring the LORD with the firstfruits and the barns being filled with plenty.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch says an offering brought quickly is answered quickly, but a man who piles up lamps and gives no honest judgment gains nothing. What God asks for is a clean heart, and the offerings only test what is in it.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 46
summaryBullets: Hear, my people, and take in the words of my lips. (46:1).

If any one bring any gifts to an earthly ruler, and have disloyal thoughts in his heart, and the ruler know this, will he not be angry with him, and not refuse his gifts, and not give him over to judgment? (46:2).

Or (if) one man make himself appear good to another by deceit of tongue, but (have) evil in his heart, then will not (the other) understand the treachery of his heart, and himself be condemned, since his untruth was plain to all? (46:3).
And when the Lord shall send a great light, then there will be judgment for the just and the unjust, and there no one shall escape notice. (46:4).
crossRefs: Malachi 1:8-9: Offer the blind and the lame to your governor and see whether he will be pleased with you or accept your person.
Proverbs 21:27: The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination, and how much more when he brings it with a wicked mind.
Proverbs 26:23-26: Burning lips with a wicked heart are like a potsherd covered with silver dross, and hatred covered by deceit is shewed before the whole congregation.
Luke 8:17: Nothing is secret that shall not be made manifest, neither anything hid that shall not be known and come abroad.
Ecclesiastes 12:14: God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good or whether it be evil.

translationNotes.note: Approaching a king with a present was the ordinary way to petition him, so the picture would have been familiar rather than strange. Malachi 1:8 runs the same test in reverse, asking whether a governor would accept the blind and lame animals being brought to God.

The Hebrew for flattery is built on the word for smooth. Psalm 55:21 says his words were softer than oil yet they were drawn swords, and Proverbs 26:28 says a flattering mouth works ruin. The picture is a polished surface with something underneath it.

Judgment arrives here as light rather than as fire, and its work is exposure. Isaiah 9:2 has a people in darkness see a great light, and 1 Corinthians 4:5 speaks of the Lord bringing to light the hidden things of darkness.
The Greek verb means to be hidden or to go unnoticed, and the English word latent comes from it. Luke 8:17 makes the same claim in different words, that nothing hidden shall fail to be known.

The address shifts here from my children to my people, widening the audience from the household to everyone Enoch will shortly be told to summon. From this point the instruction runs as public teaching rather than a father's advice at home.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch argues from ordinary life. A king who spots a disloyal gift refuses it and hands the giver over, and a flatterer is found out by the man he is flattering. When the Lord sends a great light, nobody will pass unnoticed.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 47
summaryBullets: And now, my children, lay thought on your hearts, mark well the words of your father, which are all (come) to you from the Lord's lips. (47:1).
Take these books of your father's handwriting and read them. (47:2).
For the books are many, and in them you will learn all the Lord's works, all that has been from the beginning of creation, and will be till the end of time. (47:3).

And if you will observe my handwriting, you will not sin against the Lord; because there is no other except the Lord, neither in heaven, nor in earth, nor in the very lowest (places), nor in the (one) foundation. (47:4).

The Lord has placed the foundations in the unknown, and has spread forth heavens visible (physical) and invisible (spiritual); he fixed the earth on the waters, and created countless creatures, and who has counted the water and the foundation of the unfixed, or the dust of the earth, or the sand of the sea, or the drops of the rain, or the morning dew, or the wind's breathings? Who has filled earth and sea, and the indissoluble winter? (47:5).
I cut the stars out of fire, and decorated heaven, and put it in their midst. (47:6).
crossRefs: Deuteronomy 4:39: Know therefore this day that the LORD he is God in heaven above and upon the earth beneath, and that there is none else.
Genesis 22:17: Thy seed shall be as the stars of the heaven and as the sand which is upon the sea shore, the two things nobody counts.
Psalm 24:1-2: The earth is the LORD's and the fulness thereof, for he founded it upon the seas and established it upon the floods.
Job 38:28-30: Hath the rain a father, and who hath begotten the drops of dew, and out of whose womb came the ice.
Psalm 147:4-5: He tells the number of the stars and calls them all by their names, and his understanding is infinite.

translationNotes.note: The list runs heaven, earth, the lowest places and the foundation, which are the four levels this book laid out in its creation account: light above, the world between, the deep below, and the base underneath everything.

translationNotes.term: He fixed the earth on the waters
translationNotes.note: Psalm 24:2 says he founded it upon the seas and established it upon the floods, and Psalm 136:6 says he stretched out the earth above the waters. The book is restating the arrangement its own creation chapters described, with rock piled up out of the waves.

translationNotes.term: I cut the stars out of fire
translationNotes.note: The speaker switches to God in the first person in the last line of the chapter with nothing to mark the change. That switching runs through the second half of the book, where Enoch repeats what he was told and the quotation marks are not there.

Sand and stars are the standing pair for a number nobody can reach, used at Genesis 22:17 for the promise to Abraham and at Hosea 1:10 for the same idea. This chapter drops them into a list with raindrops and dew for the same effect.

One Hebrew word carries wind, breath and spirit together, so a phrase about the wind breathing is not a figure of speech in the original but the plain use of the word. John 3:8 turns on exactly that double sense in Greek.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch tells his sons to read the books he wrote and says there is no other God anywhere, above, below or in between. He then piles up what nobody can count: the water, the dust, the sand, the raindrops, the dew and the breathings of the wind.

stories.title: 📜 2 Enoch (Secrets of Enoch) 48
